## 🔒 Permanent protocol applied

This Issue now follows the repository-wide Coder Request Protocol.

For this request and every future major request:
1. The Coder must execute the full checklist.
2. After finishing, the Coder MUST return to this same Issue and fill a completion ledger with **STATUS + one-line result + evidence** for every requirement.
3. A later Coder may continue the same Issue and must preserve/extend that ledger.
4. The Coder's "DONE/COMPLETE" is only a claim.
5. I will independently read the Issue, comments, ledger, commits, repository state and runtime evidence after the Coder reports completion.
6. Only my independent verification can mark the work as actually verified.
7. Missing, PARTIAL, BLOCKED, PENDING or unverified rows keep the request open.

# DEEP UPSTREAM SOURCE MINING — 50+ REAL CANDIDATES, SOURCE-LEVEL AUDIT, AND MAXIMUM REUSE

This is a continuation of this existing master issue, NOT a new parallel campaign. Preserve the prior inventories and evidence. The goal is to discover reusable code, algorithms, tests, data, and engineering knowledge that could eliminate substantial MiniAndroid work, then prove what is actually reusable against the current repository. Do not merely produce a list of links or claim “research complete.”

## 0. Read the current source of truth first — mandatory

Before changing code or repeating research, read and reconcile at CURRENT remote HEAD:
- `.agent/CODER_REQUEST_PROTOCOL.md` and the repository constitution / laws / campaign state / worklog;
- existing `docs/UPSTREAM_CODE_INVENTORY.md`, `docs/UPSTREAM_AVAILABLE_NOT_USED.jsonl`, `docs/UPSTREAM_RUNTIME_USAGE.jsonl`, `docs/UPSTREAM_LICENSE_MATRIX.jsonl`, `docs/UPSTREAM_UPDATE_TRACKING.jsonl`, `docs/UPSTREAM_REPLACEMENT_PLAN.jsonl`;
- current root registries, loading compatibility matrix, existing root census (#376), Kotlin/Compose external-runtime experiment (#379/#380), current base-first and execution-family issues (#383/#384), and latest source files referenced by those records;
- current `git remote -v`, branch, HEAD SHA, worktree status, recent commits, build identity, and available evidence. Do not trust a prior HEAD or copied status as current.

Existing research already concluded that changing the VM alone does not remove the Android framework bridge cost; Robolectric/Paparazzi/Roborazzi and related tools are primarily oracles/test infrastructure; and full Android OS environments (Anbox/Waydroid/redroid/Cuttlefish) are not equivalent to a lightweight host runtime. Revalidate against current evidence; do not reopen settled questions without new source evidence.

## 1. Source candidate seed list — 50 real projects/source trees

These are leads, NOT claims that all are directly reusable. Inspect actual code, tests, build graph, license and integration boundaries. Some are reference implementations or test oracles only. Do not count duplicates/forks as independent evidence.

### APK/container, manifest/resources, DEX/class loading
1. **AOSP libandroidfw / AssetManager2** — https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/a319bd3c2329/libs/androidfw/AssetManager2.cpp — inspect `ApkAssets.cpp`, `LoadedArsc.cpp`, `AssetManager2.cpp`, `ResourceTypes.cpp`, `ConfigDescription.cpp`; resource table/configuration/dynamic references/cache.
2. **AOSP aapt2** — https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/master/tools/aapt2/ — compiled resources, binary XML, resource table contracts and test fixtures.
3. **Androguard** — https://github.com/androguard/androguard — APK/DEX/AXML/ARSC parsing and analysis; independent parser/oracle.
4. **androguard/axml** — https://github.com/androguard/axml — Python AXML/ARSC parser and tests.
5. **androguard/axml-parser** — https://github.com/androguard/axml-parser — Rust AXML/ARSC parser, optional Python bindings.
6. **REAndroid/ARSCLib** — https://github.com/REAndroid/ARSCLib — Java ARSC read/write/modify implementation based on AOSP structures.
7. **iBotPeaches/Apktool** — https://github.com/iBotPeaches/Apktool — APK resources, manifest decoding, framework/resource edge cases.
8. **google/smali** — https://github.com/google/smali — DEX format, parser, assembler/disassembler, integration tests and opcode behavior.
9. **dex2jar** — https://github.com/pxb1988/dex2jar — DEX/JVM conversion and format-handling ideas; assess whether useful without class-identity loss.
10. **JADX** — https://github.com/skylot/jadx — DEX parsing, control-flow, instruction decoding, debug metadata; primarily analysis/oracle, not runtime.
11. **androguard/apk-parser** — https://github.com/androguard/apk-parser — APK metadata, multidex names, manifest and entry-point extraction.
12. **google/bundletool** — https://github.com/google/bundletool — APK sets, split APKs, targeting and install-set semantics.
13. **AOSP libcore ClassLoader** — https://android.googlesource.com/platform/libcore/+/master/ojluni/src/main/java/java/lang/ClassLoader.java — delegation and class identity contracts.
14. **AOSP BaseDexClassLoader/DexPathList** — https://android.googlesource.com/platform/libcore/+/master/dalvik/src/main/java/dalvik/system/BaseDexClassLoader.java and https://android.googlesource.com/platform/libcore/+/master/dalvik/src/main/java/dalvik/system/DexPathList.java — DEX/native-library path behavior.
15. **AOSP ART** — https://android.googlesource.com/platform/art/ — ClassLinker, verifier, invoke kind, class initialization, DexCache, arrays, runtime-generated methods and executable semantic tests.

### Complete or partial APK runtimes, virtualization, native loading
16. **Lunaria** — https://github.com/yui0/lunaria — inspect `src/apk.c`, `src/loader.c`, `src/dvm/`, `src/jvm/`, `src/linker/`, `src/arm_exec.cpp`, `PROGRESS.md`; APK/XAPK/APKS/AAB, providers/activity startup, DEX and tracing. Important caveat: its native path is largely ARM guest execution; MiniAndroid ordinary corpus priority is x86/x86_64.
17. **Android Translation Layer (ATL)** — https://gitlab.com/android_translation_layer/android_translation_layer — standalone ART/Bionic/API/JNI translation feasibility; evaluate build/dependency closure, not just README.
18. **Windroid** — https://github.com/Kotoamatsukami233/Windroid — experimental Windows C++ APK runtime, DEX/AXML/ARSC/interpreter/stubs; inspect real tests and limitations.
19. **VirtualApp** — https://github.com/asLody/VirtualApp — APK/classloader/resources/component virtualization patterns; distinguish host-Android reflection hooks from host-independent code.
20. **DroidPlugin** — https://github.com/DroidPluginTeam/DroidPlugin — plugin APK lifecycle/resources patterns; native-code limitations are explicitly relevant.
21. **apkenv** — https://github.com/thp/apkenv — historical Android game compatibility layer; mine only still-valid generic algorithms and tests.
22. **A2OH/westlake** — https://github.com/A2OH/westlake — host-side runtime/bridge experiment; inspect existing findings and use as evidence, not assume full Android compatibility.
23. **A2OH/dalvik-universal** — https://github.com/A2OH/dalvik-universal — inspect executable DEX path and bridge boundary.
24. **AndroidRecomp** — https://github.com/AndroidRecomp/AndroidRecomp — native recompilation and ABI applicability; do not classify as ordinary DEX runtime unless code proves that.
25. **DroidVM** — https://github.com/Droid-VM/DroidVM — determine whether any component is an app execution backend or merely VM manager.
26. **Skydnir** — https://github.com/Skydnir/Skydnir — inspect execution capabilities and code/test maturity.
27. **droidsaw** — https://github.com/droidsaw/droidsaw — DEX analysis/decompilation versus executable-runtime boundary.
28. **QEMU** — https://github.com/qemu/qemu — CPU/system emulation and instrumentation primitives; quantify operational cost and scope.
29. **Dynarmic** — https://github.com/nih-at/dynarmic — dynamic ARM recompiler; likely not applicable to x86-native app execution, classify honestly.
30. **Unicorn Engine** — https://github.com/unicorn-engine/unicorn — CPU emulation for bounded guest/native code probes; not an Android framework.
31. **crosvm** — https://github.com/google/crosvm — virtual machine infrastructure; classify as full-guest alternative, not a lightweight framework implementation.
32. **Waydroid** — https://github.com/waydroid/waydroid — full Android-container architecture and graphics pipeline diagnostics; not a source to import wholesale.
33. **redroid** — https://github.com/remote-android/redroid-doc — Android in container/full OS option; distinguish deployment alternative from runtime components.

### Framework/lifecycle/testing/Compose oracles
34. **AOSP ActivityThread** — https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/tags/android-13.0.0_r69/core/java/android/app/ActivityThread.java — binding, providers, activity construction and lifecycle ordering; extract contracts, not the entire framework class.
35. **Robolectric** — https://github.com/robolectric/robolectric — shadows, framework behavior, native graphics mode and JVM test infrastructure.
36. **Cash App Paparazzi** — https://github.com/cashapp/paparazzi — layout/render screenshot oracle and resource handling; not a runtime substitute.
37. **Roborazzi** — https://github.com/takahirom/roborazzi — Robolectric-integrated screenshot tests, image diff and repeatable tests.
38. **J-Code Android** — https://github.com/blamspotdev/j-code-android — inspect actual source, scope and test assets; classify by executable behavior.
39. **AndroidX Fragment** — https://github.com/androidx/androidx/tree/androidx-main/fragment — FragmentManager/transactions/lifecycle contracts and tests.
40. **AndroidX Lifecycle** — https://github.com/androidx/androidx/tree/androidx-main/lifecycle — lifecycle state/observer behavior and tests.
41. **AndroidX Core** — https://github.com/androidx/androidx/tree/androidx-main/core — compatibility helpers, resources, insets and API contracts.
42. **AndroidX Compose UI** — https://github.com/androidx/androidx/tree/androidx-main/compose — composition/layout/draw semantics and tests; identify exact module and API, avoid importing a large runtime blindly.
43. **Compose Multiplatform** — https://github.com/JetBrains/compose-multiplatform — cross-platform rendering and semantics; determine if any isolated host-independent algorithms help.
44. **OpenJDK** — https://github.com/openjdk/jdk — java.util/lang/reflection/collections behavior and tests where MiniAndroid shadows host Java; verify Android divergences before reuse.

### Text, graphics, images, animation, storage, web/native helpers
45. **Skia** — https://github.com/google/skia — Canvas/path/paint/text rasterization and golden tests; build size/dependencies matter.
46. **AOSP Minikin** — https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/minikin/ — Android font collection, line-break and layout behavior.
47. **HarfBuzz** — https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz — text shaping and glyph positioning.
48. **FreeType** — https://github.com/freetype/freetype — font rasterization.
49. **ICU** — https://github.com/unicode-org/icu — Unicode, BiDi, locale and script properties.
50. **libpng** — https://github.com/pnggroup/libpng — PNG decoding/encoding.
51. **libjpeg-turbo** — https://github.com/libjpeg-turbo/libjpeg-turbo — JPEG decoding.
52. **libwebp** — https://github.com/webmproject/libwebp — WebP decoding.
53. **libavif** — https://github.com/AOMediaCodec/libavif — AVIF decode/encode; only if corpus demonstrates need.
54. **libyuv** — https://github.com/lemenkov/libyuv — pixel format conversion/scaling.
55. **Lottie Android** — https://github.com/airbnb/lottie-android — animation format and rendering semantics; Android-dependent wrapper versus portable core.
56. **Samsung rlottie** — https://github.com/Samsung/rlottie — portable C++ Lottie renderer with CMake/Meson build.
57. **FFmpeg** — https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg — media demux/decode; large dependency surface, only use if needed.
58. **minimp3** — https://github.com/lieff/minimp3 — small standalone MP3 decoder.
59. **stb** — https://github.com/nothings/stb — small image/font/audio helpers; check format coverage and license.
60. **SQLite** — https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite — storage semantics and test corpus; compare existing real SQLite/WAL path before replacing.
61. **SDL** — https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL — portable input/window/audio primitives; likely host boundary/oracle, not Android semantics.
62. **Yoga** — https://github.com/facebook/yoga — flexbox layout engine; compare against Android measure/layout before considering any use.
63. **litehtml** — https://github.com/litehtml/litehtml — embeddable HTML/CSS layout engine.
64. **Lexbor** — https://github.com/lexbor/lexbor — HTML/CSS parser/tooling; potential WebView diagnostic, not JavaScript engine.
65. **resvg** — https://github.com/linebender/resvg — SVG renderer and tests; compare Android VectorDrawable semantics carefully.
66. **NanoSVG** — https://github.com/memononen/nanosvg — small SVG parser/rasterizer.
67. **libzip** — https://github.com/nih-at/libzip — ZIP container access; compare with current in-process APK ZIP implementation.
68. **zlib** — https://github.com/madler/zlib — compression primitives and tests.

The list intentionally contains 68 leads so weak or duplicate candidates can be rejected without falling below the required 30–50 meaningful audited candidates. Expand with newly discovered projects, source files, tests, specs, issue discussions, commits, patches, and non-English sources. Do not treat stars/README claims as evidence.

## 2. Search strategy — must be genuinely broad

Use multiple query families and languages, not repeated “Android emulator” searches:
- Semantic laws and first-divergence terms: `ClassLinker`, `DexCache`, `invoke-interface`, `class initialization`, `DexPathList`, `AssetManager2`, `LoadedArsc`, `ResTable_config`, `AssetManager.addAssetPath`, `FragmentTransaction.commit`, `InnerClass STATIC`, `ServiceLoader`, `CanvasDrawScope`, `AndroidComposeView`, `ViewRootImpl`, `MeasureSpec`, `invalidate propagation`, `TextView StaticLayout`, `PathParser`, `Drawable.ConstantState`, `WindowInsets`, `Looper Handler`, `ContentProvider Cursor`, `SharedPreferences`, `Parcel`, `JNI`, `dlopen linker namespace`, `APK split install`, `x86_64 ABI`.
- Search exact exception text, symbols, function names, filenames, code snippets, regression tests, git history, PRs/commits and issue discussions. Search upstream AOSP, GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg, SourceHut, mailing lists, bug trackers, Stack Overflow only as a discovery lead, and Chinese/Japanese/Korean/Russian/other-language terms where relevant.
- Include standalone code files, test fixtures, test vectors, specs, build files, patches, gists and knowledge documents, not just repositories.
- Search project-local code before proposing a library; detect already-vendored, host-linked, adapted, available-but-unused, duplicate, abandoned, inaccessible, or irrelevant code.

## 3. Mandatory audit per candidate (all rows)

Create/extend a machine-readable registry (JSONL preferred) plus readable summary. For each candidate record:
1. Canonical URL, exact repo/file/path/symbol/test/commit/line range and date/revision inspected.
2. License and attribution obligations, license compatibility, patent/notices if applicable; **no code copying before review**.
3. Language, build system, supported host OS/CPU, dependencies, transitive dependency closure, memory/disk/build cost and whether it can run CPU-only on our current environment.
4. Actual capability demonstrated from source/tests, not README alone; version/API coverage and maintenance/activity.
5. Category: **DIRECT_REUSE**, **SMALL_PORT/ADAPT**, **SEMANTIC_REFERENCE**, **TEST_ORACLE**, **FIXTURE/DATA**, **TOOL_ONLY**, **FULL_OS/VM_ALTERNATIVE**, **DUPLICATE**, **UNAVAILABLE**, or **REJECTED**.
6. Exact MiniAndroid subsystem and integration point (files/functions/types/call path), current local implementation, duplicate effort avoided, and why it may or may not fit architecture.
7. Minimal reproducible experiment or conformance test; expected output; positive and negative control; time/cost; evidence location.
8. Decision and confidence, unresolved risks, maintenance/update strategy, and precise next action.
9. Search queries and rejected candidates, so the search can be reproduced and does not restart from zero.

At least 30 distinct candidates must be fully audited to the standard above; target 50 audited candidates. The 68 seeds are a starting pool, not an automatic pass. Avoid counting forks or multiple files in one project as separate projects, though exact source files should be separately cited.

## 4. Prioritize by potential hours saved and root fan-out

Rank by a transparent score: demonstrated applicability to an existing generic root; amount of implementation replaced; number of app families affected; portability and dependency closure; test quality; license/maintenance; integration cost; regression risk. Produce separate rankings for:
- immediate low-risk reuse;
- high-value algorithm/semantic port;
- oracle/test-only;
- long-term architectural alternatives;
- reject/defer.

Investigate especially:
- APK ZIP + multidex/split set + binary manifest/ARSC/configuration/resource lookup;
- class loader identity/delegation, DEX parsing/verification/invoke/arrays/class init;
- Application/provider/Activity lifecycle, Fragment transaction and saved-state ordering;
- Java/libcore reflection/collections/ServiceLoader/coroutines behavior;
- Android resources, drawables, XML inflater, dimensions/density, theme/config changes;
- View measure/layout/draw/invalidate/input/hit testing and frame scheduling;
- Canvas/path/clip/transform/shader/bitmap pixel behavior;
- text shaping, bidi, fallback fonts, glyph positions, line breaks and Arabic/Persian;
- Compose/CanvasDrawScope without assuming a full external Compose runtime will work;
- file paths, streams, file descriptors, SharedPreferences, SQLite/WAL, URI/Cursor/ContentProvider;
- JNI/native ELF/dlopen only for ABI-compatible x86/x86_64 targets in the ordinary campaign;
- images, vectors, animation, audio and WebView/HTML5 only where actual corpus evidence shows value.

## 5. Architecture and test constraints

- MiniAndroid is a generic host-side Android compatibility runtime, not an app-specific patch collection. No per-app hacks or blank-screen “success”.
- Ordinary app/game waves prioritize APKs whose native ABI is x86/x86_64. ARM/ARM64-only APKs are recorded as prerequisite/ABI mismatch, not misreported as the primary runtime root. Native-emulation projects may still be studied as a separate bounded alternative.
- No paid APIs, VPS, cloud GPU or mandatory hardware/KVM. Favor CPU/headless and fast low-RAM scans. Avoid vendoring large dependencies without a measured benefit.
- AOSP is semantic authority; use aapt2 and independent parsers for resource truth; real Android/emulator/device screenshots where available for visual truth; Robolectric/Paparazzi/Roborazzi for test oracles only. Tools must not silently become runtime dependencies.
- Preserve current architecture unless a bounded experiment proves a better alternative. No wholesale ART/Compose/AOSP transplant proposal without a buildable dependency-closure and measured experiment.
- Do not modify runtime code merely because a library looks promising. First establish current behavior and a minimal test; then implement only if the experiment proves a root-level generic improvement.
- Source → algorithm → semantic law → synthetic test → real APK → second independent APK/family → three-run regression. Keep status vocabulary: IMPLEMENTED / TESTED / OBSERVED / PARTIAL / BLOCKED / PENDING / SUPERSEDED. Distinguish source inspection from build-tested and runtime-tested results.

## 6. Required outputs

1. `docs/UPSTREAM_SOURCE_MINING_REPORT.md` — readable report with executive summary, search methodology, ranked shortlist, exclusions, integration cost, and honest limitations.
2. `docs/UPSTREAM_SOURCE_MINING.jsonl` — one structured record per audited candidate, exact evidence links and closed vocabulary.
3. Update existing upstream inventory / available-not-used / license / update-path files instead of creating parallel competing registries; reconcile counts and canonical IDs.
4. A “top 10 hours-saved” shortlist with exact code paths and a bounded experiment for each; at least 3 experiments should be attempted where the current environment allows, not just proposed.
5. For any direct/adapted code, add license/NOTICE/attribution and record exact upstream revision, patch delta, and upstream update strategy.
6. Add minimal tests/conformance fixtures for any port. If a candidate is only an oracle, add a differential test or fixture rather than runtime dependency.
7. Final matrix of all candidates with status, score, evidence, disposition and next action; count audited vs rejected vs pending. Do not call the campaign complete while required rows are missing.
8. Final same-issue completion ledger: every requirement must have STATUS + one-line result + evidence path/URL. Include current HEAD, build identity, commands, exit codes, test names, run hashes, screenshot SHA/metrics where visual behavior is claimed, and regression results.

## 7. Evidence gates / no false closure

For each implementation experiment:
- Record current HEAD and clean/dirty worktree, build command and binary hash.
- Read exact upstream source and relevant tests; cite exact file/function/line/commit.
- Write a minimal synthetic test with positive and negative controls.
- Run relevant existing gates and at least one real external APK when feasible.
- Use the current x86/x86_64-native corpus; record package/version/APK SHA256/ABI.
- For rendering, require actual app draw provenance/state transition/ViewTree plus screenshot metrics/SHA and three repeatable runs; a PNG alone, build success, APK parse, zero exit code, or “nonblank” image is not proof of compatibility.
- Rebuild after changes and re-run golden/negative/cross-family regression gates. Report regressions and blockers honestly.
- The coder must return to THIS issue and fill every ledger row. “Done” in chat or an unsubstantiated issue label is not evidence. The owner will independently inspect comments, commits, registries and runtime artifacts.

## 8. Stop conditions

Do not:
- create a new issue for work already covered here or #376/#379/#380;
- import whole projects just because they are open source;
- conflate emulator/VM/container/full Android OS with a host compatibility runtime;
- count README claims, stars, search snippets or unexecuted builds as proof;
- treat ARM-only execution as an ordinary x86_64 runtime failure;
- invent source locations, tests, URLs, commits, license status, results or time saved;
- close existing roots or promote statuses without evidence;
- spend waves on broad implementation before current HEAD, prior work and existing registries are reconciled.

## Definition of success

A reproducible source-backed inventory of at least 30 fully audited, distinct candidates (target 50), a ranked evidence-backed shortlist of code that can genuinely save implementation time, a set of bounded experiments with results, reconciled project registries, and independently checkable cross-app regression evidence. If no candidate is safe to import, the result must still deliver reusable semantic laws, tests, fixtures, exact upstream patches and a justified rejection—not an empty “no reuse possible” conclusion.

# ADDENDUM — SEARCH FOR ALREADY-SOLVED MINIANDROID ROOTS

This addendum answers a specific question: for roots that took substantial debugging effort in MiniAndroid, did an upstream project, specification, issue thread, Q&A, or source comment already explain the answer? **Yes, for several semantic laws.** These sources can shorten discovery, but they do not prove the same root is fixed locally; local first-divergence traces and regression tests remain mandatory.

## Case 1 — F-NEW-271 / Dooz: a null collection element became an empty String

**Local evidence in the project’s #383 continuation:** an ArrayList used by the Compose path legally contained null entries. MiniAndroid’s parallel collection representation conflated null with the empty string; remove(0) returned STRING_REF "" instead of typed null. That caused a downstream getClass NPE and aborted measure/layout before placement/draw. The generic fix introduced a distinct null-element kind across collection writers/readers, not a Dooz-specific patch or a new ArrayList implementation. The local ledger reports plain-Java ArrayList tests K19/K20 changed FAIL/FAIL → PASS/PASS and the downstream failing PC disappeared; the Dooz visual root was still blocked later, so this did not by itself fix the screen.

**Was the answer already written? Yes — the underlying contract is explicit in Java/OpenJDK collection semantics.**
- OpenJDK ArrayList source: https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/master/src/java.base/share/classes/java/util/ArrayList.java
- Java API contract: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/util/ArrayList.html
- The collection permits null; get/remove return the element actually stored. Null must not be reified as a different object/string.
- This is not a single Stack Overflow answer for MiniAndroid’s exact internal representation; it is an established semantic answer that should be found by searching the observed mismatch (“ArrayList null element returned as empty string”, “typed null lost in collection shadow”), not only “Android emulator”.

**Mining lesson:** search the violated language/runtime law first, then look for a portable implementation/test.

## Case 2 — F-NEW-277 / Dooz: Compose recomposition starved at a frame-pump “quiescence” boundary

**Local evidence in #383:** the pump treated “no work due right now” as quiescence even though future-dated dispatcher work was queued. The Recomposer runner never woke; composition #2 (navigation destination) never began. A targeted change aligned the pump with the message-queue law; the next divergence was then in invalidation delivery. The report explicitly says real app-owned pixels were still NOT produced at that stage.

**Was the answer already written? Yes — AOSP MessageQueue implements this distinction.**
- AOSP source: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/b267554/core/java/android/os/MessageQueue.java
- In MessageQueue.next(), if the head message exists but now < msg.when, AOSP sets nextPollTimeoutMillis to the future due time and waits; it does not treat that state as an empty queue. Only msg == null takes the “No more messages” path.
- Current source: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/heads/main/core/java/android/os/MessageQueue.java
- The next stage also requires Compose source: Recomposer / AndroidUiDispatcher / GlobalSnapshotManager and their tests, not just generic Android framework source.

**Mining lesson:** search the exact state predicate (“queue nonempty but head not due”, “future-dated work treated as idle/quiescent”, “recomposer runner not awakened”). Generic “Compose blank screen” search is too broad.

## Case 3 — F-NEW-264c: collection operations silently skipped for a DEX-defined subclass receiver

**Local evidence in #379:** a collection operation on a guest class extending ArrayList/LinkedList missed a declaring-class string gate; addAll became a silent no-op. The local fix used runtime subtype dispatch and was tested on guest→shadow and guest→guest paths.

**Was the general answer already written? Yes — Java inheritance/virtual dispatch and upstream collection implementations define the rule.**
- OpenJDK ArrayList: https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/master/src/java.base/share/classes/java/util/ArrayList.java
- OpenJDK AbstractCollection: https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/master/src/java.base/share/classes/java/util/AbstractCollection.java
- Java Language Specification, classes/inheritance: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se21/html/jls-15.html
- The exact MiniAndroid receiver bridge is project-specific, but behavior follows the actual receiver type/virtual dispatch; a string comparison against the declaring class is not a valid substitute for subtype-aware dispatch.

**Mining lesson:** search “subclass override dispatch shadow bridge no-op”, “runtime receiver class vs declaring class”, and upstream JDK tests.

## Case 4 — composeStopwatch / R-NEW-466: ServiceLoader iterator and Kotlin coroutine providers

**Was the answer already written? Yes — a focused upstream issue, implementation and API contract exist.**
- kotlinx.coroutines issue #1231: https://github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.coroutines/issues/1231
- Kotlin MainDispatchers: https://github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.coroutines/blob/master/kotlinx-coroutines-core/jvm/src/internal/MainDispatchers.kt
- FastServiceLoader: https://github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.coroutines/blob/master/kotlinx-coroutines-core/jvm/src/internal/FastServiceLoader.kt
- Android ServiceLoader contract: https://developer.android.com/reference/java/util/ServiceLoader
- Issue #1231 explains that the exact two-argument ServiceLoader.load + class constants + .iterator() call shape matters for R8 optimization. The source also documents fallback behavior and why provider loading can fail.
- This does not prove issue #1231 is the same MiniAndroid interpreter defect; it is a high-quality semantic/test source for provider iteration and Android optimization constraints.

**Mining lesson:** when the stack names a library, search that library’s own issues/source, not only AOSP or emulator repositories.

## Case 5 — BMI/FragmentTransaction: “must be a public static class to be properly recreated”

**Was the answer already written? Yes — multiple Q&A answers and AndroidX source explain the contract.**
- Stack Overflow: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/39295458/fragment-must-be-a-public-static-class-to-be-properly-recreated-from-instance-state
- Another direct example: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/39978924/fragment-null-must-be-a-public-static-class-to-be-properly-recreated-from-instance-state
- AndroidX Fragment source/tests: https://github.com/androidx/androidx/tree/androidx-main/fragment
- FragmentManager may recreate a Fragment from saved state. An anonymous/local or non-static inner class requires an enclosing instance and cannot be recreated through the default path; a Kotlin inner class has the analogous issue. Use an accessible independently-instantiable class/default constructor, or a configured FragmentFactory. Pass ordinary state through arguments.
- For MiniAndroid, the app may intentionally contain an invalid Fragment class. The runtime must implement the exception/validation contract, not silently “fix” the app by inventing an enclosing instance.

## Case 6 — R-NEW-461 WindowInsets.CONSUMED and compatibility behavior

**Was there existing source? Yes.**
- AndroidX WindowInsetsCompat implementation: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/support/+/bfa9192be525fe763aa47c7b99d5b29578d4688b/core/core/src/main/java/androidx/core/view/WindowInsetsCompat.java
- It explicitly attempts to reflect WindowInsets.CONSUMED and has fallback logic for older API levels, documenting the API-availability issue.
- Local roots still need local probe/consumer proof; this source is a compatibility implementation to mine, not automatic proof of equivalence.

## Source classes missing from the previous repository-only seed list

Add these problem-solving source classes to the methodology:
1. Exact upstream unit/conformance tests, often more useful than implementation prose.
2. Git history and bug-fix commits, including parent commit and regression test.
3. Stack Overflow/issue threads with accepted answers, used as discovery evidence then checked against authoritative source.
4. Java Language Specification, Java API contracts, Android API docs and AndroidX compatibility implementations.
5. Library-specific issue trackers for Kotlin/coroutines, Compose, Fragment, Navigation, graphics and resource loading.
6. Exact exception strings and stack frames, including mapping obfuscated symbols to the APK’s pinned dependency source.
7. Differential tests between independent implementations (OpenJDK vs Android libcore; AOSP vs AndroidX; AAPT2 vs independent ARSC parsers).
8. Historical commits fixing the same semantic class and tests that prevent regression.

## Required action on this master task

For each high-effort local root in the current registry and recent CONT reports:
- Extract exact symptom, first divergence, subsystem, local fix and investigation path from project evidence.
- Search exact exception/symbol, then a language/API contract query.
- Search upstream source, tests, issues, PRs and commit history.
- Classify the result as EXACT_MATCH / SAME_SEMANTIC_LAW / RELATED_ONLY / NO_MATCH_FOUND.
- Capture exact source/test/issue/commit and what is reusable (implementation, test, fixture, or explanation).
- Compare the local fix against the upstream source; estimate whether it could have shortened discovery, implementation or validation.
- Never claim a source answer fixes the local root until first-divergence evidence and regression tests agree.

Prioritize F-NEW-271 null element, F-NEW-277 scheduler/quiescence, F-NEW-264 collection subtype dispatch, Compose invalidation delivery after F-277, ServiceLoader/provider identity, Fragment class-instantiation rules, resource/configuration lookup, and Canvas/Text/path semantic mismatches.

This addendum is source-backed discovery, not a claim that all listed roots are independently verified at current HEAD. Re-read local wave evidence and current HEAD before changing statuses.

# PROBLEM-FIRST FOLLOW-UP — HISTORICAL ROOTS WITH UPSTREAM ANSWERS ALREADY PRESENT

This follow-up records additional findings from MiniAndroid's wave evidence and targeted source searches. It is not a claim that external sources alone prove a local fix; each match still needs current-HEAD first-divergence and regression gates.

## Finding A — F-NEW-272: null default Thread.UncaughtExceptionHandler in the Dooz crash-report path

### Local problem recorded in CONT-20 / #383
After F-NEW-271 was fixed, the Dooz chain advanced beyond the null-element failure. The next reported divergence was the app's own crash-report path calling UncaughtExceptionHandler.uncaughtException when the default handler was null; the reporter then threw and propagated to the app boundary. The local ledger labels F-NEW-272 as a missing Thread default-handler law.

### Was the answer already written? YES — directly in AOSP RuntimeInit
- Android 10 RuntimeInit: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/%2B/refs/heads/android10-c2f2-release/core/java/com/android/internal/os/RuntimeInit.java
- Current AOSP RuntimeInit: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base.git/%2B/master/core/java/com/android/internal/os/RuntimeInit.java
- Android 15 RuntimeInit: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/%2B/refs/tags/android-15.0.0_r1/core/java/com/android/internal/os/RuntimeInit.java

In RuntimeInit.commonInit(), Android installs a LoggingHandler as the uncaught-exception pre-handler and calls Thread.setDefaultUncaughtExceptionHandler(new KillApplicationHandler(loggingHandler)). The implementation explains that apps may replace the default handler, while the pre-handler is retained. This is the exact bootstrap location to inspect for the missing behavior.

### Important semantic boundary
Do NOT implement “Thread's default handler can never be null” as a universal Java rule. The Java API permits a null default handler; Android's process bootstrap installs its own handler. The generic root candidate is therefore ANDROID_PROCESS_BOOTSTRAP_UNCAUGHT_HANDLER, not a blanket change to Thread semantics. The minimal correct experiment should compare:
1. fresh host-JVM Thread semantics before Android bootstrap;
2. MiniAndroid process after its intended bootstrap stage;
3. app calling Thread.setDefaultUncaughtExceptionHandler(null) or installing a custom handler;
4. uncaught exception on main and worker threads, including handler failure;
5. Android pre-handler vs default-handler ordering and process-boundary behavior.

Potential time saved: high for identifying the right source and initialization point; the actual bootstrap implementation must be adapted to MiniAndroid's architecture and must not import internal process-kill behavior blindly.

## Finding B — Compose invalidation delivery has ready-made upstream race tests

The Dooz chain has distinct stages: future-dated queue work, snapshot notification, Recomposer invalidation, recomposition, applying changes, LayoutNode measure/place, then draw. The project notes correctly warn not to collapse these into one “Compose is broken” root.

High-value upstream sources/tests:
- Recomposer implementation: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/support/%2B/refs/heads/androidx-main/compose/runtime/runtime/src/commonMain/kotlin/androidx/compose/runtime/Recomposer.kt
- JVM race test recompositionOnConcurrentSnapshotInvalidation: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/support/%2B/0624f640fd3a47edfcf8a070f609d278fb5eb41b/compose/runtime/runtime/src/nonEmulatorJvmTest/kotlin/androidx/compose/runtime/RecomposerTests.jvm.kt
- Composition pending-modification drain: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/support/%2B/a0e356f1a1a2e704a6bc447bfb2a1dc786b751d3/compose/runtime/runtime/src/commonMain/kotlin/androidx/compose/runtime/Composition.kt
- Subcomposition invalidation regression test (b/320385076): https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/support/%2B/b0e5b2829bdf1aa4e1f9ded4e845d942aa224c3c/compose/runtime/runtime/src/nonEmulatorCommonTest/kotlin/androidx/compose/runtime/CompositionTests.kt
- Historical Compose Desktop race fix (GlobalSnapshotManager / sendApplyNotifications / frame clock): https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/support/%2B/e64d5e742fd90ee3ddc72829d945ba5fed0804fa

The JVM race test deliberately creates a concurrent invalidation window and checks that pending work is not lost. The historical desktop commit documents a real race among GlobalSnapshotManager, sendApplyNotifications and frame-clock delivery. These are far more useful than copying a Compose runtime wholesale: adapt the race shape into a small independent synthetic probe, then map it onto MiniAndroid's actual call/queue/state trace.

Classification: SAME_SEMANTIC_LAW / TEST_ORACLE, not proven exact match. Do not import the Compose runtime as a runtime dependency.

## Finding C — the Fragment failure has a historical source commit, not only Q&A

Exact authoritative source and history:
- Current FragmentTransaction implementation: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/support/%2B/ffe9335a155bf0dea9c3558e50da01d526579040/fragment/fragment/src/main/java/androidx/fragment/app/FragmentTransaction.java
- Historical commit adding the more specific exception: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/support/%2B/05ed14f5c36546bd171efdd99282c19231289669

The source explicitly checks anonymous/non-public/non-static-member Fragment classes; the historical commit “Improve Exception message for adding private fragments” records the code change and bug ID 29565251. This is stronger than relying on Q&A alone: it gives the exact implementation and historical change. The source should become a reflection/modifier conformance fixture for MiniAndroid, including public top-level, public static nested, non-static inner, anonymous, private nested, and Kotlin-inner analogues.

## Methodological correction from these cases

A search of only emulator/runtime repositories would likely miss all three answers. Search in this order:
1. exact local symptom/stack frame and first incorrect value;
2. Android/Java semantic contract;
3. bootstrap/framework/library source where that contract is established;
4. upstream regression tests and bug-fix commits;
5. local synthetic positive/negative probe;
6. real APK and cross-family regression.

Add each item to the canonical existing upstream inventory (do not create duplicate registries) with categories, exact revision, license, MiniAndroid integration point, and match confidence. F-NEW-272 is the strongest direct lead; Compose is a high-quality test-oracle lead; Fragment is an exact contract/source-history lead.

## Completion ledger for this addendum
- AOSP RuntimeInit exact bootstrap call found: OBSERVED — source links above.
- Compose invalidation race/test sources found: OBSERVED — source/test links above.
- Fragment exact implementation + historical fix commit found: OBSERVED — source/commit links above.
- Current MiniAndroid runtime re-tested by this research pass: NOT TESTED.
- Claims that these external sources fix current HEAD: NOT CLAIMED.

# INDEPENDENT ROOT-BY-ROOT RESEARCH — MORE ANSWERS ALREADY EXIST OUTSIDE EMULATOR REPOS

I read the project's own CONT-11/20/22 evidence and searched the actual first-divergence symptoms, not only runtime project names. These are additional findings to merge into the existing upstream inventory. Some sources give an exact semantic law; others are test oracles, not proof that the same defect exists at current HEAD.

## 1. F-NEW-265 / Dooz: null CharSequence reaches Compose text-layout construction, then exception handling fails to stop the frame

**Local historical evidence:** #379 CONT-11 says the measure/layout chain dies because Lm7.<init> receives a null text CharSequence; the Kotlin-generated null check throws, but MiniAndroid's deferred-throw behavior continues executing the throwing frame, creating multiple NPEs and eventually a null Throwable at a Compose report helper. Placement is never completed (isPlaced=false), so draw is skipped. This is materially different from a Canvas bridge bug.

### External answers found
- Compose TextLayoutInput API: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/support/+/08d5daf3743f7863d6e20ca00fa6bda4d62d5bfd/compose/ui/ui-text/api/current.txt
- Compose CanvasDrawScope implementation (later draw-stage reference): https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/support/+/130b63ba39383c22791068aaf04e290ee6e93a9f/compose/ui/ui-graphics/src/commonMain/kotlin/androidx/compose/ui/graphics/drawscope/CanvasDrawScope.kt
- ART interpreter implementation: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/art/+/master/runtime/interpreter/interpreter_switch_impl0.cc
- ART verifier MOVE_EXCEPTION rule: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/art/+/master/runtime/verifier/method_verifier.cc

**Conclusion:** the upstream text API is a contract/reference, but the strongest reusable answer is ART's exception model. Once a Kotlin null check throws, execution must follow DEX exception dispatch; it must not continue ordinary instructions in the throwing path, and a move-exception handler receives the actual pending Throwable. ART source explicitly treats exception state as pending at MOVE_EXCEPTION and carefully preserves/restores it around instrumentation. This makes the local deferred-exception issue a high-priority semantic root to compare against ART, not a text-rendering patch.

**Suggested bounded probe:** a synthetic DEX method where a null check throws, with (a) no catch, (b) matching catch, (c) non-matching catch, (d) finally/catch-all, (e) a second throw while handling the first. Compare exact PC, handler entry, move-exception object identity, and whether subsequent side effects ran. Then repeat with the existing Dooz trace. Do not treat null text itself as proof the engine should silently substitute an empty string; preserve app semantics and determine why null was produced.

## 2. F-NEW-265: isPlaced=false is downstream, and Compose has explicit placement state-machine code

- LayoutNode.isPlaced definition: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/support/+/8a179e4d865a33584667c68c736c276e558d275d/compose/ui/ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/androidx/compose/ui/node/LayoutNode.kt
- Placement state transition in MeasurePassDelegate: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/support/+/76d0b0fea265ed90a4ea030b0bc54e0f9fcf522d/compose/ui/ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/androidx/compose/ui/node/MeasurePassDelegate.kt
- Official Compose layout ordering: https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/layouts/basics

These sources show placement is a state transition performed during layout, not a drawing flag to force true. Local evidence says placement writers were never reached because measure unwound first. Therefore do not patch isPlaced, call draw regardless of placement, or bypass the measure exception. Target the first throwing frame; use placement sources as an oracle to verify the tree naturally reaches placement and draw after the fix.

## 3. F-NEW-264d: six plain-Java collection semantic failures can be mined from OpenJDK

CONT-11 lists 15 failing rows grouped into six laws: read-your-mutation coherence, iterator write-back, Java 8 default methods, deque views, hash view coherence, and missing subList/Stream families.

Direct sources:
- OpenJDK AbstractList (iterator/listIterator/subList delegate through get, set, add, remove): https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/master/src/java.base/share/classes/java/util/AbstractList.java
- OpenJDK Collection (default removeIf, stream, parallelStream, toArray and collection contracts): https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/master/src/java.base/share/classes/java/util/Collection.java
- OpenJDK AbstractCollection: https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/master/src/java.base/share/classes/java/util/AbstractCollection.java
- Java Collection API: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/util/Collection.html

**What is already answered:** these are documented algorithms/contracts, including which methods delegate to iterators and how default methods behave. For each of the six local failure clusters, compare the shadow bridge against the exact JDK method body and turn the relevant contract into a small conformance test. Do not port all of java.util wholesale or close the cluster merely because one representative row passes.

## 4. R-NEW-414 / F-NEW-274: zero-object creation must not invent an object whose constructor captures are missing

CONT-22 found a precise law: an R8 merged-lambda class had no no-arg constructor; the runtime fabricated a zero-object, leaving captured field .f null and defeating the app's own null guard. The local class_has_no_arg_ctor() gate was tested and produced cross-family benefit (Dooz and OpenCalc).

Add regression fixtures for (a) a type with a real no-arg constructor, (b) only parameterized constructor/captured fields, (c) uninitialized allocation followed by constructor invocation, and (d) constructor throws. The law is “do not manufacture a successfully initialized instance when no valid construction path exists.” Avoid generic fallbacks that mask required initialization.

Related authoritative sources:
- ART verifier/execution source: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/art/+/master/runtime/verifier/method_verifier.cc
- Java Language Specification, class instance creation: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se21/html/jls-15.html

Classification: SAME_SEMANTIC_LAW. The local CONT-22 fix is already reported ROOT-CAUSED+FIXED; verify against current HEAD before reopening.

## 5. URI-null / ContentResolver: Android API contract gives a precise negative test

Known pending root family in #376: memory/zip/WebView path and URI-null.

- AOSP ContentResolver.openInputStream: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/android-7.0.0_r33/core/java/android/content/ContentResolver.java
- Android API reference: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/content/ContentResolver

The method requires a non-null Uri and accepts content:, android.resource:, and file: schemes. It can return null when a provider has recently crashed, so “non-null Uri” and “non-null returned stream” are different contracts. Build a conformance matrix: null Uri; unsupported scheme; missing file/resource; provider returns null; valid content URI; close/error propagation. This prevents conflating input-null with a valid-but-null stream result.

## 6. S-2 dlopen/JNI/native-surface campaign: loader rules are already documented in source

Known pending root family in #376/#379: dlopen/JNI/native surface, with x86/x86_64 as normal target ABI priority.

- AOSP libnativeloader README: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/system/core/+/show/e99728fcf2ffac572fbd4babcad19898352cf7be/libnativeloader/README.md
- Namespace implementation: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/system/core/+/1e40c30b0cc0f2ae007dacc64fe08af52cc731e3/libnativeloader/library_namespaces.cpp
- Android NDK JNI guidance: https://developer.android.com/ndk/guides/jni-tips

These sources explain that System.loadLibrary is associated with the calling classloader's namespace, app-local JNI directories and public-library allowlists; JNI FindClass uses classloader context and behaves differently on an attached native thread without app frames. Split the native root into independent laws: ABI/ELF compatibility, library path selection, namespace visibility, JNI_OnLoad classloader context, RegisterNatives vs symbol lookup, and JNI thread attachment. Do not treat an ARM-only library as a normal x86_64 runtime failure.

## 7. WorkManagerInitializer: the exact manifest metadata shape is upstream-visible

- AndroidX WorkManager manifest: https://github.com/androidx/androidx/blob/androidx-main/work/work-runtime/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml
- AndroidX Startup source: https://github.com/androidx/androidx/tree/androidx-main/startup/startup-runtime/src/main/java/androidx/startup

The merged manifest declares androidx.startup.InitializationProvider and androidx.work.WorkManagerInitializer metadata. For the local pending provider-meta-data root, compare the APK's actual merged/binary manifest and PackageManager flags with this upstream shape; do not invent a provider if it is not declared. The runtime should faithfully return declared provider metadata and let the app/library handle missing declarations as Android does.

## Required update to the existing inventory (do not create a parallel registry)
Add rows for:
- F-NEW-265: ART exception dispatch = semantic-law lead; Compose TextLayoutInput and MeasurePassDelegate = API/state-machine oracle.
- F-NEW-264d: AbstractList/Collection = implementation and conformance-test source for six local semantic clusters.
- R-NEW-414/F-NEW-274: constructor/captured-field initialization = regression-fixture law; local fix already reported tested, verify at current HEAD.
- URI-null: ContentResolver input/output null distinction = direct API contract.
- S-2 dlopen/JNI: libnativeloader/JNI tips = architecture reference, subdivide by ABI/path/namespace/classloader law.
- WorkManagerInitializer: AndroidX merged manifest = fixture/manifest oracle.

For every row record exact local evidence path, local commit/HEAD verified, upstream pinned revision, license, direct-vs-reference classification, minimal test, affected target families, and estimated time saved. Keep estimates qualitative unless supported by historical time logs.

## This pass's honest status

# FOUNDATION 1/4 — THE VIEW INVALIDATION → TRAVERSAL → DRAW CONTRACT (HIGH-FAN-OUT BASE GAP)

This is one narrowly scoped foundational area, selected from the actual current project records. It must be audited/fenced before spending another wave on application-specific white screens. Do not generalize it into a new giant renderer rewrite.

## 0. Evidence that this is a real unresolved base gap in OUR repo

- Existing issue **#288 / MG-116 “invalidate propagation” is still OPEN**: https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/issues/288
- Its description states: current render-path properties are implemented, but dedicated law tests are pending.
- The currently fetched `docs/MICRO_GAP_REGISTRY.json` records MG-116 as:
  `STATUS=PARTIAL`, `EVIDENCE=""`, `TEST=""`, `FANOUT=not_measured`, note “render-path properties implemented (S94 transform laws); dedicated law tests pending”.
- Contrast with **#242 / MG-115 requestLayout propagation**, which the repository records as fixed/closed at commit `7a0a8dab`: a real DEX-driven requestLayout no-op was fixed and the named S106 stage passed. **Do not reopen MG-115 or conflate requestLayout with invalidate.**
- Recent Compose reports (#383 CONT-23/25) have a separate scheduler/invalidation chain. This card targets the classic Android View invalidation contract first. Reuse existing ViewRoot/traversal evidence and keep Compose-specific invalidation as a separate path.

The key problem is not yet proven to be “invalidate is entirely broken”. The grounded defect in the repository evidence is that this base contract is still PARTIAL and lacks its dedicated law fence. We need to close that uncertainty with one minimal, high-fan-out probe, before choosing any code fix.

## 1. Exact upstream answer already exists (no vague web-research assignment)

### A. View.invalidateInternal — child dirty state and parent propagation
AOSP current source:
https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/master/core/java/android/view/View.java

Exact path: `View.invalidate()` → `invalidate(boolean)` → `invalidateInternal(l,t,r,b,...)`.

Source law:
- Reject/no-op invalidations where the view's existing state makes invalidation unnecessary.
- Mark the view dirty and invalidate/cache-clear flags as required.
- If the View has both a parent and AttachInfo and the damage bounds are non-empty, set the dirty Rect and call `ViewParent.invalidateChild(this, damage)`.
- `invalidate()` is redraw-only: onDraw is scheduled for a future point; layout is not automatically requested. For a non-UI thread the public contract directs callers to `postInvalidate()`.

A historical source excerpt with the complete method is also available at:
https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/5be83ed/core/java/android/view/View.java

### B. ViewGroup — descendant invalidation is a recursive hierarchy contract
AOSP current source:
https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/master/core/java/android/view/ViewGroup.java

Exact symbol: `ViewGroup.onDescendantInvalidated(View child, View target)`; compare the legacy `invalidateChild` / `invalidateChildInParent` path too.

Source law:
- Dirty state must propagate through parent groups to the root.
- Animation dirty flags and cache validity matter.
- Software layers can require escalation to a full parent invalidation.
- Hardware-accelerated path can ignore dirty rectangles because RenderThread computes damage; do not impose one software-only dirty-rectangle rule on every backend.
- A child mutation is not enough by itself: the right ancestor/root path must be notified.

### C. ViewRootImpl — one pending traversal must actually reach performTraversals
AOSP Android 12 source:
https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/android12-release/core/java/android/view/ViewRootImpl.java

Exact symbols: `requestLayout()`, `onDescendantInvalidated()`, `invalidate()`, `scheduleTraversals()`, `doTraversal()`, `performTraversals()`.

The current source explicitly shows `scheduleTraversals()` setting the scheduled bit and posting `Choreographer.CALLBACK_TRAVERSAL`, and `doTraversal()` consuming the scheduled state before entering `performTraversals()`:
https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/master/core/java/android/view/ViewRootImpl.java

Core law: coalesce repeated invalidations into a pending traversal, but never lose the pending work. A traversal already in progress may consume changes in that traversal; mutations after the relevant phase may require a subsequent pass. Queue non-empty-but-future-due work must not be misclassified as quiescence (the AOSP MessageQueue law that already fixed a separate F-277 scheduler issue).

## 2. Why this foundational root has broad fan-out

This is a shared contract for text updates, custom Views, canvas games, widgets, drawable state changes, animations, pressed/selected/checked visual states, and many layouts. If state changes but invalidation never reaches the root, the app may execute Java/Kotlin normally while continuing to display an old or background-only frame. This is cheaper to investigate generically than creating app-specific redraw patches.

It is distinct from:
- MG-115 requestLayout (now closed; geometry/measurement must be recalculated);
- resource decode (whether bytes/images were loaded);
- Canvas draw semantics (whether draw commands/pixels are correct);
- Compose Recomposer invalidation (app-Dex Compose semantics);
- Surface/BufferQueue presentation (whether already-produced pixels reach the final target).

## 3. Minimal synthetic law probe — required before any patch

Add a dedicated, named stage to the existing battery. Use real engine/framework objects and a DEX-built fixture where the existing test architecture allows. Do not mock the propagation chain.

Fixture:
- Root ViewGroup → nested ViewGroup → custom child View.
- Child onDraw paints a unique known color at a fixed region and records a draw counter.
- Root/parent/child record layout and measure counters and invalidation/traversal markers.
- Start from a captured baseline. Change only the child's internal state and call `invalidate()`.
- Run one bounded frame pump and capture the new frame.

Required rows:
1. Child `invalidate()`: subsequent app-owned draw runs and final pixels change from color A to color B; measure/layout counts do **not** increment solely because of invalidate.
2. Nested grandchild invalidates: dirty/draw state reaches root, not just immediate parent.
3. Repeated invalidations before a frame: coalesced into a traversal, but latest state is drawn (no lost update).
4. `requestLayout()` control: the known MG-115 law still triggers measure/layout; do not count it as an invalidate pass.
5. Detached child: no false claim that it reached an attached root; after attach, a fresh invalidate must draw.
6. Visibility/state control: hidden/GONE behavior follows Android law; changing visibility or reattaching must not permanently suppress a future visible invalidation.
7. Transform/scroll control: transformed child damage uses the correct parent/root coordinates in the software path; hardware path checks dirty-state propagation without incorrectly requiring the same rectangular damage optimization.
8. Software-layer parent versus hardware-accelerated path: cache invalidation and ancestor propagation must not silently diverge.
9. Negative control: change child data without invalidation and without another pending frame; prove that the engine is not merely redrawing everything on every call and hiding broken invalidation.
10. Invalidate from a non-UI thread must follow the supported `postInvalidate` path; test UI-thread contract separately rather than broadening invalidate's semantics.

For each row record:
- first marker absent/wrong;
- dirty flags / parent receiver;
- whether scheduleTraversals equivalent was requested/coalesced;
- whether traversal ran;
- child onDraw invocation;
- app-owned pixel delta / screenshot SHA;
- measure/layout deltas;
- exact binary identity and status.

Expected first-divergence categories:
A. child never marks dirty;
B. child marks dirty but parent chain stops;
C. root receives invalidation but no traversal is scheduled;
D. traversal is scheduled but the frame pump doesn't execute it;
E. traversal/draw executes but the child draw is skipped due to bounds/visibility/dirty flags;
F. drawing occurs but no pixels reach the framebuffer/presentation stage.
Do not fix stage F if the first failure is B or C.

## 4. Real APK fan-out after the synthetic stage

Use the current actual green base, not a historical binary or assumed HEAD:
- one real View-based app (OpenCalc or equivalent existing anchor);
- one Canvas/View game (ballbreak or equivalent x86/x86_64-native anchor);
- one drawable/text-bearing app with interactive visual state (existing verified corpus target);
- keep Dooz as a separate diagnostic control, not the sole success criterion.

Run at least 3 fresh executions after a proven fix, use a state-changing tap where possible, and prove the expected app-owned pixel delta as well as screenshot identity. Existing green anchors must remain byte-identical where their behavior should not change.

## 5. Required implementation discipline

- First fetch current remote HEAD and inspect the live `View.invalidate`, parent propagation, frame pump, and test battery paths. Do not rely on historical file locations or statuses alone.
- Compare the existing code against the AOSP symbols above. Report exact MiniAndroid function/file/line for every divergence.
- If probe passes, do not invent a fix. Add the dedicated law fence, measure fan-out, and close MG-116 only with test/commit/evidence.
- If it fails, change only the earliest divergent generic primitive. No package-name checks, no forced draw, no always-full-screen redraw as an unmeasured workaround, and no bypass of visibility/placement rules.
- Re-run canonical battery, verified screenshot anchors, and a family sweep. Capture process exit status immediately after engine invocation; previous project audit caught shell code that accidentally overwrote `$?`.
- Update the existing MG-116 ticket, `docs/MICRO_GAP_REGISTRY.json`, relevant source registries and worklog. Do not create a duplicate root/issue.

## 6. Required same-issue ledger
Post the completed STATUS — RESULT — EVIDENCE rows here in #364 and link the MG-116 closing/progress evidence:
- current HEAD / worktree / binary SHA;
- exact AOSP revision/symbols compared;
- local paths/functions compared;
- each synthetic row before/after and positive/negative control;
- first divergence (if any);
- real APK package/version/SHA/ABI and 3-run evidence;
- battery result and golden hashes;
- fan-out demonstrated vs merely predicted;
- status: IMPLEMENTED / TESTED / OBSERVED / PARTIAL / BLOCKED / PENDING / SUPERSEDED.

Do not close this request because “invalidate appears to work”. The success criterion is a dedicated passing law test proving a View child's state mutation reaches a root traversal and changes app-owned pixels without spuriously forcing measure/layout, plus cross-family no-regression evidence.

Research status of this card: **SOURCE-FOUND + LOCAL-GAP-CONFIRMED (MG-116 PARTIAL)**. Current code/runtime was not changed or re-run by this research pass; no local fix is claimed.

# OPERATING CONTRACT — “CONTINUE 364” = RESEARCHER + CODER CLOSED-LOOP, BASE-FIRST

This is a standing workflow contract for the owner, ChatGPT/researcher, and the primary coder. It is not a new implementation wave and not permission to change architecture without evidence. It exists to convert external knowledge into verified generic runtime improvements, while preventing repeated searches, speculative fixes, and app-specific patches.

## 1. Trigger / continuation rule

When the owner says **“ادامه 364” / “CONTINUE 364”**:

### Researcher (ChatGPT) must
1. Read the newest comments in THIS issue before doing new research, including the last numbered FOUNDATION card and coder feedback.
2. Re-check current repo evidence through GitHub: root registries, existing issue history, worklog, source/replacement registries, and current dispositions. Do not treat old HEADs/statuses as current.
3. Choose exactly ONE next high-fan-out, still-open foundation problem. Prefer a demonstrated unresolved base contract affecting many independent APK families, not another app-specific symptom.
4. Find the external answer personally: exact upstream source symbol, implementation, conformance test, bug report, accepted technical answer, historical fix commit, or minimal reusable algorithm. Search problem-first using the local symptom, stack, first bad value and semantic rule—not only project names.
5. Cross-match against our repository so already-fixed, already-tested, duplicate, environment-only and out-of-profile items are not reopened.
6. Post one self-contained, actionable research card as a comment in this same issue. Do not merely tell the coder “research X”, and do not create a parallel issue for a root already tracked elsewhere.
7. In the card, cite links and exact symbols/revisions where available; explain the mechanism, local comparison point, expected first divergence, minimal probe, positive/negative control, target-family fan-out, regression gates and remaining uncertainty.
8. Wait for the coder's evidence before calling an external lead successful. On later continuation, read that evidence first, mark the lead appropriately and select the next unresolved base root.

The researcher does not run MiniAndroid binaries in this workflow and must never claim a runtime fix was verified without coder evidence.

### Coder must
1. Treat each newest FOUNDATION card in #364 as supplied research intelligence, not as a vague topic.
2. Before work, fetch current remote HEAD and confirm clean/dirty state, read the specific card, relevant local source, current registry rows and relevant prior issue evidence. Report if the cited root is already fixed or if HEAD differs materially.
3. Read the cited upstream source/test at the pinned revision. If the supplied source is stale or the symbol moved, provide the replacement source URL/revision; do not silently substitute a different contract.
4. Map the external mechanism to exact MiniAndroid file/function/class/dispatch path. State whether the match is EXACT_MATCH, SAME_SEMANTIC_LAW, RELATED_ONLY, DUPLICATE, ALREADY_FIXED, ENVIRONMENT_ONLY, OUT_OF_PROFILE, or NO_MATCH_FOUND.
5. Reproduce the smallest relevant semantic law before changing code. Use real engine objects where possible, with positive and negative controls. Do not implement merely because an external bug resembles the symptom.
6. Fix only the first causal generic divergence that the probe identifies. No package-name checks, app-specific conditionals, forced draw, fake pixels, unconditional polling, “swallow the exception” shortcuts, or broad rewrite unless the owner explicitly changes the architecture decision after measured evidence.
7. Prove fan-out, not just progress within one app: at least one representative target for the original root and a second independent app/family or a formal conformance suite. Prefer the currently verified x86/x86_64-compatible corpus for ordinary APK execution.
8. Run three fresh executions for any result used to accept a fix. Preserve exact APK identity/version/SHA/ABI, binary SHA, command, exit code, first-divergence traces, test names, screenshot SHA/metrics and cross-family golden/battery deltas.
9. If current environment cannot test the target, mark BLOCKED with the exact missing prerequisite; never convert it to PASS/TESTED. Build success, rc=0, no crash, an existing PNG, ViewTree presence, decode success or draw() invocation alone are not rendering success.
10. Update the canonical existing registry and worklog; avoid duplicate root IDs and duplicate source registries. Close/update the specific underlying issue if its protocol requires that, but always report the result back in THIS #364 thread.

## 2. Mandatory result loop — this is how the researcher learns what worked

After every foundation card, coder MUST post a comment in **this #364 conversation**, even if no source change was made. Do not leave results only in local files, a different issue, chat, or a commit message.

Use this exact result schema:

```text
FOUNDATION CARD: <number/title>
STATUS: VERIFIED / IMPLEMENTED+TESTED / PARTIAL / BLOCKED / DUPLICATE / ALREADY_FIXED / REJECTED
CURRENT HEAD: <full SHA>
BINARY SHA256: <full SHA>
LOCAL ROOT/ISSUES: <IDs and links>
UPSTREAM MATCH: EXACT_MATCH / SAME_SEMANTIC_LAW / RELATED_ONLY / NO_MATCH_FOUND
UPSTREAM SOURCE: <URL + commit/tag + file:symbol/test>
LOCAL PATH: <file:function/class:line>
FIRST DIVERGENCE: <exact event/value/PC or NONE>
HYPOTHESIS: <one sentence>
SYNTHETIC PROBE: <name, positive control, negative control, before/after>
CAUSAL RESULT: <intervention and evidence or NOT TESTED>
REAL TARGET A: <package/version/APK SHA/ABI, result>
INDEPENDENT TARGET B: <package/version/APK SHA/ABI or formal conformance source, result>
THREE-RUN: <three run IDs and result hashes, or BLOCKED/PENDING>
PIXEL/STATE PROOF: <app-owned draw ops, state delta, pixel metrics and screenshot SHA, or NOT APPLICABLE with reason>
REGRESSION: <battery/anchors/family sweep, exact deltas>
CHANGES: <commit and diff paths, or NO CHANGE>
REGISTRY/WORKLOG: <canonical files/rows updated>
WHY THIS SAVES BASE WORK: <proved fan-out or explicitly UNMEASURED>
REMAINING UNCERTAINTY: <what isn't proved>
NEXT BEST BASE ROOT: <one candidate + reason>
```

The coder must explicitly separate:
- SOURCE_FOUND — an external source exists;
- OBSERVED — local behavior was seen;
- REPRODUCED — a minimal test recreates the problem;
- ROOT-CAUSED — causal intervention isolates it;
- IMPLEMENTED — code changed;
- TESTED — the named tests ran and passed;
- VERIFIED — required independent target/family and regression evidence passed.

These are not interchangeable. Do not promote status based on a source link or a plausible explanation alone.

## 3. Research card quality gate

Each researcher card posted in #364 must contain:

A. **Local proof of why this root is still worth investigating**: current/local registry row, incomplete evidence/test, pending frontier, or exact historic first-divergence report. Clearly label historical versus current-HEAD evidence.

B. **External answer**: exact AOSP/ART/AndroidX/OpenJDK/library source, authoritative API/compatibility contract, source test, historical bug-fix commit, or a directly relevant accepted answer. Prefer source + test/commit over blogs. Include license when actual code copying is proposed.

C. **Mechanism**: explain why the bug happens causally, not only that it happened elsewhere.

D. **Exact local comparison point**: current MiniAndroid call path and symbol/file to inspect; if not yet known, say precisely what must be found and which trace proves it.

E. **Minimal probe**: synthetic positive and negative controls, the expected first-divergence signature, and a causal intervention that can falsify the hypothesis.

F. **Generic fan-out**: name distinct app families that may benefit and distinguish measured beneficiaries from expected ones.

G. **Disposition and stop condition**: existing root reused, candidate, duplicate, already-fixed, environment prerequisite, rejected, or verified. State what evidence would make us stop pursuing the lead.

Bad card: “Investigate rendering / Compose / images.”
Good card: “AOSP symbol X sets state Y then schedules callback Z. Our local registry has row R marked PARTIAL because test T is missing. Check function F; if event sequence A occurs but B never occurs, this hypothesis is supported; if B occurs, reject it. The probe must assert C and fail under negative control D.”

## 4. Base-first priorities

Rank candidate work by:
1. number of independent APK families affected, measured if possible;
2. whether the issue lies on the common execution path (resource/class loading, object identity, thread/exception, lifecycle/window/view, layout/draw, dispatcher/state, input, storage/provider, native loader);
3. whether upstream source provides a direct algorithm and tests;
4. amount of app-specific workaround code it could eliminate;
5. reproducibility and ease of a bounded causal test;
6. integration/dependency/license cost and regression risk.

Prefer one generic semantic law that eliminates many failures over closing multiple individual app launch errors. A root that only advances Dooz to another log line is not automatically a win; only the measured shared primitive matters.

Keep these boundaries explicit:
- classic View invalidation/traversal ≠ Compose snapshot/Recomposer invalidation;
- resource lookup ≠ decode ≠ draw ≠ raster ≠ presentation;
- requestLayout/measure ≠ invalidate/draw;
- DEX class loading ≠ native library loading;
- application API semantics ≠ full Android OS/system-server/graphics-compositor availability.
Reuse current positive real-APK anchors as regression controls, but confirm they are genuinely app-owned pixels/state-change proofs rather than deterministic white-screen captures.

## 5. Android contracts and source code: what can be reused?

Yes—AOSP/ART/AndroidX source and tests can save substantial effort when used as the specification for the behavior being reproduced. Android's Compatibility Definition Document says documented APIs must have their documented behavior and should not be silently replaced by no-ops except where explicitly allowed:
https://source.android.com/compatibility/11/android-11-cdd.pdf
Android platform testing guidance also distinguishes API conformance tests (CTS) from implementation/regression tests:
https://source.android.google.cn/docs/core/tests?hl=en

But these contracts are not a drop-in runtime. Copy code only after checking exact Android/API revision, dependency closure, host portability, license, build and target profile. Often the greatest saving comes from porting one small algorithm or one conformance test, not importing a whole subsystem. The source is the answer to “what should this do”; local probes prove “what is MiniAndroid actually doing”.

## 6. What the owner should see after each “continue 364”

- Researcher posts exactly one next foundation card to #364.
- Coder reads that card, tests/refutes it and posts the structured evidence result to #364.
- At the next “ادامه 364”, the researcher MUST read the latest coder result and use it to decide the next root. Verified leads become canonical knowledge; falsified hypotheses are recorded so nobody repeats them.
- Never claim the loop succeeded until the coder's #364 result comment is visible and the evidence can be inspected.
- Never create a new broad issue just to avoid the standing contract. Use the same #364 thread as the shared research/verification ledger; update the existing specific root issue/registry as needed.

## 7. Initial state of this contract

- FOUNDATION 1/4: classic View invalidate → root traversal → draw; supplied in #364. MG-116 is the specific existing PARTIAL lead; MG-115 requestLayout is already recorded closed and must not be reopened.
- FOUNDATION 2/4: Compose Recomposer work-wakeup/snapshot invalidation; supplied in #364. The external Stack Overflow answer and official AndroidX Recomposer source are leads; exact local causal match still needs the coder's probe.
- The next “ادامه 364” should read those two cards and any coder response first, then deliver FOUNDATION 3/4 only after cross-matching the live registry.

This contract is considered adopted only when the coder acknowledges it in this #364 thread and follows the result schema for subsequent cards.
