# FOUNDATION 3/4 — INSTALLED PACKAGE IDENTITY + CANONICAL PATH / BYTE-SOURCE CONTRACT

This card follows FOUNDATION 1 (View invalidation) and FOUNDATION 2 (Compose Recomposer wake-up). It targets a separate foundation: every app-visible file/resource/code/native request must resolve to bytes belonging to the installed package and correct Android namespace—not an original sideload path, current working directory, another app's private directory, or stale cache.

**Do not rewrite the installer or path mapper first.** Existing base-APK identity proof is valuable. This card targets remaining unproven boundaries and current source-level risks with explicit falsifiable tests.

## 0. Current source-of-truth and stale-document warning

Fetched the actual GitHub default branch:
- Commit/tree: **913bc044da4d9a4294a02717fb4122a67add7eaa**
- Latest commit (2026-10-15): CONT-70 evidence-script recovery, zero engine changes.
- Current files inspected:
  - miniandroid/src/main.cpp — SHA 3db52dbabf61a0381caf90e1a03f3668072c087a
  - miniandroid/src/storage/data_root.cpp — SHA 03905c1246cf0065d582bdd1ba3b2a2cec387514
  - miniandroid/src/storage/data_root.h — SHA e6e4f7d5551a618d2267dd8aee9d0a9de7608a06
  - miniandroid/src/apk/apk_parser.cpp — SHA d740269d12ded5866237eb74a294fb969e2909a9
  - miniandroid/src/apk/apk_parser.h — SHA 938aedaecacf71ec677df061ed6434121c6a8dbf
  - miniandroid/src/resources/resource_runtime.cpp — SHA d961f7e4f227a24380837e4af21f3dc18329400c
  - miniandroid/src/framework/bitmap_shadow.cpp — SHA b19c4b836a0ca5c7b438e7e977cb98113473b437
  - miniandroid/src/diagnostics/file_io_trace.h — SHA 738f27ccd963961e77a49d45cf2d58d94f4f7f67

**Critical evidence hygiene issue:** docs/LOAD_COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX.jsonl (SHA 4da20e4af085d60ad512b19dd85d355087ee702a) still includes old claims such as missing File APIs/FDs, BitmapFactory path-mapping gaps, and broken package metadata. These conflict with later Gate-A evidence:
- docs/INSTALL_ENVIRONMENT_API_MATRIX.jsonl (SHA 4030fd8631faafb1b04400694277a574f9b6dce0): 74 rows, 70 TESTED, 1 FIXED, 1 OBSERVED, 2 HONEST-FAIL at recorded HEAD 80644b566b1c659d5f645c048ec36910a64f960c.
- docs/INSTALL_ENVIRONMENT_PROVENANCE_SCHEMA.jsonl (SHA a24a6d08ec683f6740526fec87a286a5f5b54bd8): source APK SHA equaled installed base.apk SHA; original source was moved away before package-identity launch; file/stream/FD/resource/decode probes ran.
- docs/INSTALL_ENVIRONMENT_GAPS.md (SHA d4ee76dfbe1d3e39ab256c8347bb2aab569ed195): later closeout reports ABI-scoped extraction/nativeLibraryDir and device-protected storage tested; actual native execution remains a distinct frontier.
- docs/DIFFERENTIAL_WORKING_VS_WHITE.md reports 11/11 tested package identities matched source-to-installed bytes and ran with source APK hidden; Bouncy has real asset/openFd evidence.

These old/new docs are not a single coherent current-HEAD matrix. Reconcile them; do not reopen a fixed path API just because a stale row says BROKEN, and do not copy an old PASS without re-running it.

## 1. What has already been proved — do not repeat without new contradictory evidence

### A. Ordinary base-APK identity
Current miniandroid/src/main.cpp cmd_install:
- parses and hashes the input APK;
- copies it to <data-root>/data/app/<package>/base.apk;
- hashes the installed copy and compares it to the source SHA;
- writes package.json after the copy/integrity check.

The code explicitly documents a deliberate AOSP deviation: AOSP uses randomized /data/app/~~random~~/<pkg>-random/base.apk, while MiniAndroid uses deterministic <data-root>/data/app/<package>/base.apk for inspectability. Do not change that path merely to imitate randomized Android paths.

The run --package branch constructs pkgstore::package_dir(data_root, package) / base.apk, checks it exists, prints installed-package mode/codePath, and replaces the input apk_path with the installed path. Existing Gate-A and 11-target source-hidden evidence proves source SHA == installed base.apk SHA and package identity launches still use installed bytes.

Therefore, the generic hypothesis “MiniAndroid always executes directly from the original sideload path” is already disproven for the tested base-APK cases. Do not repeat that claim.

Source: https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/blob/main/miniandroid/src/main.cpp

### B. Several consumers already use the canonical path resolver
Current miniandroid/src/framework/bitmap_shadow.cpp sends BitmapFactory.decodeFile(path) through Storage::resolve_android_path(path), denies rejected host paths, and opens the resolved backing path. Do not reuse the stale Oct 3 claim that decodeFile opens the raw caller string; it has been changed.

The later installation matrix also has tests for ordinary Context directories and I/O, AssetManager.open/list, stored openFd, AssetFileDescriptor byte equality, ParcelFileDescriptor lifecycle, openRawResource, BitmapFactory decodeResource/decodeFile/decodeByteArray, and ABI-scoped native extraction. Compressed openFd returning FileNotFoundException is the intended Android contract, not a loading bug.

Sources:
- https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/blob/main/miniandroid/src/framework/bitmap_shadow.cpp
- https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/blob/main/docs/INSTALL_ENVIRONMENT_API_MATRIX.jsonl
- https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/blob/main/docs/INSTALL_ENVIRONMENT_PROVENANCE_SCHEMA.jsonl

## 2. Candidate P0-A — path resolution may identify a package by path shape without enforcing caller identity

### Exact current source mechanism to test
In miniandroid/src/storage/data_root.cpp:
- set_context_package(package) stores the active package in process-global g_context_package.
- resolve_android_path(logical) is described as the ONE path mapping for all app file consumers.
- For /data/data/<pkg>/..., the resolver extracts a package segment and maps it to <root>/data/data/<pkg>/... when the name contains a dot.
- For /data/user/<id>/<pkg>/..., it extracts user ID and package and maps user 0 to CE storage and other user IDs to their backing directories.
- These branches do not visibly compare the requested package or user to g_context_package or a permission/share decision before returning allowed=true.
- For any relative string, the function currently builds package_data_dir() / logical and returns allowed=true without a containment check inside that function.
- The /storage/emulated/0 dispatch uses a prefix test rather than an explicit end-or-slash component-boundary check.

These are concrete source-level risk candidates, not yet claims of a reproduced runtime exploit. Verify all actual call sites and any upstream checks before classifying them as live defects. Do not fix by simply denying every non-running package path: PackageManager, shared resources, or an explicit content grant may legitimately resolve a different package under a defined policy. The required law is caller identity + API-specific access policy + canonical namespace.

### Exact upstream references
AOSP ContextImpl obtains package-owned directories from the active package's data-dir/ApplicationInfo fields, and getFilesDir is constructed under getDataDir:
- https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/HEAD/core/java/android/app/ContextImpl.java
- ApplicationInfo paths include sourceDir, splitSourceDirs, dataDir, deviceProtectedDataDir, credentialProtectedDataDir and nativeLibraryDir:
  https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/master/core/java/android/content/pm/ApplicationInfo.java
- Current MiniAndroid mapper:
  https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/blob/main/miniandroid/src/storage/data_root.cpp
- MiniAndroid path law:
  https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/blob/main/miniandroid/src/storage/data_root.h

### Required bounded tests
1. Package A creates a unique private file under /data/data/A/files. Read it through A's supported aliases, then attempt the same path from a DEX fixture running as package B. Expected: A succeeds; B gets the correct denial/absence unless a documented grant/API explicitly permits access.
2. Repeat with /data/user/0/A/files, /data/user_de/0/A/files, another user ID and another package. CE aliases must agree; DE must remain physically distinct; cross-package/user boundaries must not be bypassed by the host process's broad OS identity.
3. Relative-path matrix with ., .., repeated separators and deeply nested traversal: a relative path may navigate only according to the declared Android API semantics and must never escape the approved app namespace to the package-store parent or host files. Test read and write.
4. Test storage mount boundaries: /storage/emulated/0/file vs /storage/emulated/012/file, /storage/emulated/0evil/file and unsupported mounts. A sibling prefix must not alias the primary volume.
5. Negative controls: /etc, /home, /proc, /tmp must not be accessed through app File/stream/BitmapFactory paths unless an explicit supported Android-profile mapping allows it; retain the documented /dev/urandom, /dev/random, /dev/null, /dev/zero exceptions.
6. Every row records the caller API/method, active package, requested Android-logical path, normalized path, PathCategory, physical backing path, decision/result, typed exception and actual bytes SHA when successful.

Expected first divergence: the resolver returns ALLOWED for a path escaping the app namespace/addressing another app's private root, or a real API call bypasses the canonical resolver and directly opens a host path. Do not implement a path fix until the DEX-visible path is proven and a pre-fix negative control fails.

## 3. Candidate P0-B — install/update does not visibly commit the APK and package record atomically

### Exact current code to test
In cmd_install() in miniandroid/src/main.cpp, the new APK is copied directly to the final installed path using copy_file(..., overwrite_existing); only after that does the code hash the destination and compare it with the source, and then write package.json. If the destination hash check fails, the code removes the entire package directory. If writing the package record fails after APK copy, the code returns failure but does not visibly roll the copied base.apk back.

Potential inconsistent states after a failed or interrupted update:
- Existing base.apk may be overwritten before the new package record is committed.
- A failed integrity check may remove the previous installed code directory/data-bearing package directory.
- A process exit between base.apk promotion and package.json write may leave code and registry state inconsistent.
- run --package gates primarily on base.apk existence, rather than a verified agreement between the committed record, installed SHA and version.

This is source-level evidence of a possible transactional failure path; no interrupted install was executed by this research pass.

### Compare with upstream and current code
- AOSP PackageManagerService install/reconciliation source:
  https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/master/services/core/java/com/android/server/pm/PackageManagerService.java
- Current MiniAndroid install/run implementation:
  https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/blob/main/miniandroid/src/main.cpp

### Minimal fault-injection test
Create two tiny APK versions with the same package name but distinct versionCode, manifest label, resource string, asset bytes, DEX marker and SHA:
1. Install V1; verify package record, base.apk SHA, launch marker, resource and asset bytes.
2. Attempt V2 with a deliberate failure at each commit boundary (staging copy, SHA validation, package-record write and native extraction/manifest write).
3. After every failure, run pkgaudit and run --package.
4. Expected: V1 remains wholly usable or V2 is wholly committed. Never leave mixed code/record state; never silently remove the previous valid private data tree on a failed update.
5. Successful V2 must make manifest/DEX/resources/assets agree on V2 SHA/version.
6. Hide the original source APK after install in all post-install checks.

Only if the test reproduces the inconsistent state should the implementation be changed. The likely direction is a temporary sibling staging file/directory, validation first, and an atomic promotion/recovery marker, but this is not authorization for a broad installer rewrite before the test.

## 4. Candidate P0-C — same-path cache replacement and split APK support

### A. Resource/APK cache identity
Current miniandroid/src/resources/resource_runtime.cpp starts ensure_loaded(apk_path) with the equivalent of: if already loaded and apk_path_ equals the same string, return true. When the path differs it resets theme/overlays, parses the new APK, extracts resources.arsc and rebuilds the inflater.

The same-path check does not itself detect changed file bytes when the exact installed path is replaced while the process/cache remains alive. However, ordinary CLI launches may use a fresh process, so do not claim this is a live app failure until an in-process reload/replacement scenario is demonstrated.

Test whether the runtime can replace/reload an installed package in the same process or re-enter ensure_loaded after the file at the same path changes. If impossible under the declared runtime lifecycle, mark NOT_APPLICABLE. If reachable, key cache identity to committed package generation/SHA as well as path.

Source: https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/blob/main/miniandroid/src/resources/resource_runtime.cpp

### B. Split APK remains an explicit frontier, not a base-APK failure
docs/UPSTREAM_REPLACEMENT_PLAN.jsonl still marks UPP-003 (split APKs/S-11) AVAILABLE_NOT_USED: no split fixture and no merged-table proof. Current cmd_install installs one file as base.apk, and no demonstrated committed split sibling set is established in the ordinary path.

This is a real unsupported/untested input class that can cause missing classes or resources in APKs delivered as a base + configuration/feature split set. It is not evidence that ordinary base APK installation is broken.

Authoritative laws:
- ApplicationInfo.splitSourceDirs is the ordered list of installed split APK paths:
  https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/master/core/java/android/content/pm/ApplicationInfo.java
- ResourcesManager adds the base resource path and every splitResDir into AssetManager:
  https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/HEAD/core/java/android/app/ResourcesManager.java
- AssetManager2 handles multiple ApkAssets and documents search order:
  https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/master/libs/androidfw/AssetManager2.cpp
- DexClassLoader's documented path can contain APK/JAR files with classes.dex and has a distinct librarySearchPath:
  https://android.googlesource.com/platform/libcore/+/refs/heads/master/dalvik/src/main/java/dalvik/system/DexClassLoader.java

Minimal split fixture:
- base APK declares launcher Activity;
- a required class and resource exist only in a split;
- a config split contributes a density-qualified drawable;
- test install metadata, splitSourceDirs, resources merge order, classloader visibility and source SHA for every installed APK.
Hide the original files after install; each class/resource must identify the installed split that supplied it.
If split support is outside the current release contract, issue an explicit UNSUPPORTED_SPLIT/PREREQUISITE verdict before running, not a false generic class-not-found/resource-missing root.

## 5. One end-to-end installed-byte audit across all API consumers

A successful run --package does not prove every consumer uses the same source of bytes. Inspect actual current live call paths, not declarations only:

1. Manifest, PackageInfo, ApplicationInfo: sourceDir, publicSourceDir, dataDir, CE/DE roots, splitSourceDirs, nativeLibraryDir and version/installed identity.
2. APK/DEX reader: installed base.apk path, each DEX entry name and identity hash.
3. Resources: ResourceRuntime/ARSC/AXML/LayoutInflater use installed base and split paths.
4. Assets: AssetManager.open/list/openFd/openNonAsset; record which APK cookie/path supplied each asset since split precedence matters.
5. Files/streams: File, FileInputStream, FileOutputStream, Context file APIs, external paths, canonical paths and aliases.
6. Images: BitmapFactory decodeResource/decodeFile/decodeByteArray/decodeStream consume only their designated source, no CWD/host/source-APK fallback.
7. Java class resources: ClassLoader.getResource/getResources/getResourceAsStream and Class.getResourceAsStream. Keep APK classpath resources separate from app filesystem APIs.
8. Native files: record selected ABI, extracted .so hash, nativeLibraryDir, and distinguish extraction/path success from actual dlopen/JNI_OnLoad execution.
9. URI routes: file://, content://, android.resource://, file:///android_asset/ and HTTP(S) have different owners; do not route them all to a generic file fallback.
10. Provenance: each actual open/read/list/stat path must use the canonical mapping or a separately documented archive/provider resolver.

The current MINIANDROID_FILE_IO trace records operation/path/result/caller/subsystem/package but a rigorous test must record both requested logical path and resolved physical path (or an unambiguous mapping event), package/version/source SHA, APK entry/split identity, and bytes SHA/length when meaningful.

## 6. Acceptance matrix for one deterministic test suite

Use fixed files with unique fingerprints: text token, PNG dimensions/pixel color, stored asset, compressed asset for the expected openFd negative case, ARSC string + drawable, DEX version marker, two APK versions with same package, and optionally a split-only resource/class.

Mandatory rows:
A. Source SHA == installed base.apk SHA; source hidden; executed version marker agrees with installed record.
B. /data/data/<pkg> and /data/user/0/<pkg> map to the same CE bytes.
C. /data/user_de/0/<pkg> remains physically distinct.
D. Relative paths/dot-segments cannot escape the documented app namespace.
E. Another package cannot read private data merely because the host process owns both folders; explicit grants are tested separately.
F. /storage/emulated/0 path boundary and external-storage API round trips are consistent.
G. BitmapFactory resource/file/stream and AssetManager paths prove the correct source/bytes.
H. Installed resources and DEX never silently fall back to the source APK or current working directory.
I. Failed install/update does not leave half-committed identity or destroy a known-good prior install/data tree.
J. Same-path cache replacement and split input are either tested or explicitly classified not applicable/unsupported.
K. Missing/malformed paths return the API's honest typed failure, never fake empty data/success.
L. Run three fresh trials after any claimed generic fix; preserve current good anchors, especially the prior 11 source-hidden targets and Bouncy asset/FD path.

Identify first divergence exactly: install commit, installed identity lookup, path mapping, archive entry lookup, stream/FD, resource cache, DEX/classloader, decoder, or render/presentation. Do not close a path issue because the APK happens to launch.

## 7. Required output in this Issue thread

Post results here and update the canonical existing matrices/roots, not parallel registries:
- current tested HEAD and runtime binary SHA;
- current pkgstore install/run paths verified;
- list of actual API consumers that use resolve_android_path and those that bypass it;
- results of cross-package and traversal controls;
- install fault-injection outcomes;
- same-path cache probe result;
- split support decision and fixture result;
- A/B hashes and logical/physical path records for every call;
- reconciliation commit for stale LOAD_COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX rows;
- battery, 3-run, anchor and cross-family regression evidence.

Status rules:
- VERIFIED = current-HEAD test evidence, not source inspection only.
- SOURCE-FOUND = upstream mechanism found but exact local match unproven.
- PARTIAL = some rows pass and others remain open.
- NOT_APPLICABLE = prove the path is unreachable in this runtime lifecycle.
- BLOCKED = exact missing fixture/environment/dependency.
- FIXED only when the reproducer is corrected, the negative control still fails for the correct reason, the positive case passes and cross-family regression is clean.

Do not apply a blanket path restriction, atomic installer rewrite or split loader from this source inspection alone. The strongest source-level concern is **path-shape recognition vs package identity/namespace permission**, followed by **non-transactional package replacement**. Prove reachability and the first divergence before changing code.

## Honest research status
- Current default-branch source commit inspected: OBSERVED.
- Base-APK source-hidden identity: ALREADY TESTED in previous Gate-A/11-target evidence; not rerun here.
- Runtime build/execution in this research pass: NOT RUN.
- Package-private path/traversal: SOURCE-LEVEL CANDIDATE, RUNTIME REPRO REQUIRED.
- Install/update atomicity: SOURCE-LEVEL CANDIDATE, FAULT-INJECTION REQUIRED.
- Same-path cache replacement: CONDITIONAL CANDIDATE; first prove in-process replacement is reachable.
- Split APK: explicit AVAILABLE_NOT_USED frontier UPP-003; no current fixture proof.
- No fix is claimed by this research pass.

# FOUNDATION 4/4 — DEX CLASS-INITIALIZATION STATE MACHINE (<clinit>, FAILURE, RE-ENTRY, CONCURRENCY)

## Why this is the next candidate

This is a high-leverage runtime contract, not an app-specific UI fix. A class initializer can establish static registries, Kotlin object/singleton state, framework caches, generated metadata, and other state used by many unrelated APK families. Incorrect initialization order or failure-state handling can create misleading downstream symptoms: null static fields, repeated side effects, wrong exception types, inconsistent state between threads, or a crash far away from the original initializer.

I fetched the current default-branch `docs/MICRO_GAP_REGISTRY.json` (blob SHA `b84aa999f767cc077cea897f49b50d3a8e638c10`). Its `MG-310` row currently says:
- API: `class initialization ordering`
- STATUS: `PARTIAL`
- NOTE: `implemented; dedicated fence pending`
- EVIDENCE / TEST / COMMIT: empty
- FANOUT: `not_measured`
- UPSTREAM_SOURCE: `frameworks/base/core/java/android/content/Context.java`

This is a concrete unclosed test gap, **not proof that the implementation is wrong**. The recorded Context.java upstream pointer appears too indirect for the actual VM class-initialization algorithm; correct it or justify it. Do not create a duplicate root if MG-310 already covers the same contract. This card proposes a focused law audit and fence for MG-310, not a new issue.

## 1. Exact upstream contract to verify

### Java Language Specification — initialization procedure
https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se21/html/jls-12.html#jls-12.4.2

Section 12.4.2 specifies the synchronized initialization protocol, including:
- already initialized classes return without rerunning initialization;
- recursive initialization requested by the same thread must not deadlock or rerun the initializer;
- another thread must wait while a different thread initializes the same class;
- a failed initialization leaves the class in an erroneous state;
- the first active use propagates the initializer failure under the specified wrapping rules, and later active uses must follow the erroneous-class failure behavior rather than silently retrying `<clinit>`.

Also check JLS §12.4.1 for which uses trigger initialization and the special rules for constant variables/interfaces:
https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se21/html/jls-12.html#jls-12.4.1

### Android ART implementation oracle
https://android.googlesource.com/platform/art/+/refs/heads/main/runtime/class_linker.cc

Inspect the current implementations of:
- `ClassLinker::EnsureInitialized`
- `ClassLinker::InitializeClass`
- `ClassLinker::InitializeDefaultInterfaceRecursive`
- erroneous-class handling / `ThrowEarlierClassFailure`
- class-initialization locking and visibility publication

The source explicitly refers to JLS §12.4.2 for its locking protocol. Treat ART as an Android implementation oracle; the JLS is the normative language-level contract. Do not blindly port ART internals into MiniAndroid.

## 2. Cross-match against MiniAndroid before proposing a fix

Re-read current MG-310 and the current implementation at remote HEAD. Trace the actual DEX execution path for:
- triggering class initialization before the first active use that requires it;
- executing `<clinit>` exactly once per runtime class identity;
- superclass and applicable default-method interface initialization ordering;
- recursive same-thread access during `<clinit>`;
- a second thread arriving while initialization is in progress;
- successful completion publication to later readers;
- failure transition and the behavior of subsequent active uses;
- distinction between a compile-time constant read and an active use that requires initialization.

Record the current HEAD and exact file/function/line references. Do not assume the older registry row is still current, and do not infer a defect solely from missing tests. Check whether class identity/class-loader boundaries change the expected “once” scope.

## 3. Minimal deterministic law fence

Create or reuse a real DEX fixture built through the project's accepted toolchain. Keep it small and isolate each behavior. Suggested test cases:

1. **Exactly once:** `<clinit>` increments a visible counter; repeated active uses must leave it at 1.
2. **Ordering:** superclass initializer runs before subclass initializer; add a default-method interface case where applicable.
3. **Recursive same-thread access:** initializer re-enters code that reads the class; prove no duplicate execution or self-deadlock and compare observed values with the JLS rule.
4. **Concurrent access:** two threads race to first-use the same class; the initializer executes once, the other thread does not observe partially published initialized state, and both runs terminate.
5. **Failure first use:** initializer throws a non-Error exception; verify the correct first-use exception contract, including `ExceptionInInitializerError` where required.
6. **Failure later use:** touch the same class again; verify the erroneous-class behavior (typically `NoClassDefFoundError`) and prove `<clinit>` is not retried.
7. **Error thrown directly:** test an initializer that throws an `Error`; verify wrapping/propagation matches the JLS.
8. **Initialization trigger boundary:** a constant-variable read must not spuriously initialize its declaring class; contrast with a genuine active use.
9. **Class identity boundary:** if two class loaders can define the same binary name in this runtime, verify initialization state is not accidentally shared between distinct class identities.

Use positive and negative controls. Run each relevant case three times with fresh runtime state where practical. Add a named test/battery stage and retain the canonical battery.

## 4. Evidence required

For each case, record:
- tested remote HEAD SHA and binary SHA;
- fixture source/build recipe and APK/Dex identity;
- exact command, environment, exit code;
- expected versus actual initializer event sequence;
- thread IDs and ordering evidence for concurrency cases;
- exact thrown exception type and cause chain;
- initialization count and resulting static values;
- trace showing the first divergence, if any;
- test output path/hash and regression battery result.

A successful build, process survival, or screenshot is not sufficient evidence for this semantic contract.

## 5. Decision protocol

Before code changes, classify the current state:
- `ALREADY_FIXED_AND_TESTED`
- `PARTIALLY_IMPLEMENTED_TEST_GAP`
- `CONFIRMED_SEMANTIC_BUG`
- `DUPLICATE_OF_MG-310`
- `NOT_APPLICABLE_TO_CURRENT_RUNTIME`
- `BLOCKED_NEEDS_FIXTURE/THREAD_SUPPORT`

If all tests pass, do not manufacture a bug: add the fence, update MG-310 with actual evidence and measured fan-out, and stop. If a failure is found, identify the first divergence and fix the generic class-initialization law, not an individual APK. If multithreaded execution is not sufficiently supported to test the concurrency case, record that as a bounded blocker rather than claiming concurrency compatibility.

## 6. Required continuation comment in this issue

Return to this same Issue #364 with a completion ledger:
- Current HEAD / binary SHA
- MG-310 current status and exact source path
- Each test case: `TESTED`, `PARTIAL`, `BLOCKED`, or `PENDING`
- Upstream source symbols actually inspected
- Commands and evidence links
- Before/after if a correction is justified
- Cross-app regression outcome
- Remaining uncertainties and unrun tests

Do not claim this card was executed merely because it has been posted. Keep any untested item explicitly pending.

**Goal:** establish whether the class-initialization state machine is a real generic compatibility gap, then close it with a small reusable law fence—or prove it already correct and move on.

# FOUNDATION 5/4 — NATIVE LIBRARY + JNI EXECUTION CONTRACT (UPP-001; REUSE EXISTING ROOT)

## Why this is the next high-fan-out frontier

I re-read the latest #364 comments first, including the operating contract and FOUNDATION 4/4. I then checked the current default-branch source registries rather than trusting the older card snapshots.

Current source evidence:
- `docs/UPSTREAM_REPLACEMENT_PLAN.jsonl` currently contains **UPP-001**, area `dlopen/JNI native libraries`, status `PENDING_RESEARCH`.
- Its record says there is no native `.so` loading, no APK `.so` extraction in the current end-to-end path, and the JNI bridge currently contains a HOST_COMPATIBILITY_STUB registry. It identifies the real frontier as native execution—not just the existence of a `nativeLibraryDir` string.
- The same record notes prior progress: ABI-scoped install extraction metadata, nativeLibraryDir identity, three-shape `loadLibrary` UnsatisfiedLinkError handling, and an env-gated `dlopen/dlerror` probe. Therefore **do not re-open those completed pre-native legs as if they never existed**.
- It names `miniandroid/src/dex/dalvik_engine.cpp` as the native-method resolution integration point and `miniandroid/src/jni/jni_bridge.h` as the current bridge/stub surface.
- It records a real app frontier at GodotView / Asteroids and says the remaining architectural choice—native execution compatible with the runtime—is unresolved.

This is **not a new issue and not a claim that every native APK must now run**. Reuse UPP-001 and the existing native/JNI roots. This card asks for a source-first design and a falsifiable end-to-end test of the missing execution contract.

## 1. Upstream sources and the semantic chain

### Android ART: load a native library
https://android.googlesource.com/platform/art/+/master/runtime/jni/java_vm_ext.cc

Inspect `JavaVMExt::LoadNativeLibrary`, including:
- how a library path is selected and associated with its class loader;
- how repeated loads are handled;
- how `JNI_OnLoad` is discovered and called;
- how load/initialization failures are returned;
- how native libraries and class-loader identity are tracked.

Related ART call path:
https://android.googlesource.com/platform/art/+/master/runtime/native/java_lang_Runtime.cc
Inspect `Runtime_nativeLoad`: it delegates to `JavaVMExt::LoadNativeLibrary` and converts failure to the caller-visible result. Do not infer that a successful host `dlopen` alone means Java-level loading succeeded.

### Android ABI packaging and extraction
https://developer.android.com/ndk/guides/abis
Android expects libraries in APK entries shaped like `lib/<abi>/lib<name>.so`. Installation chooses libraries for an ABI supported by the target and exposes a native library directory. A path string alone is not evidence that the library exists, has the right machine type, or can be loaded.

### JNI registration and symbol lookup
https://github.com/android/ndk/wiki/JNI
Verify the distinction between explicit `RegisterNatives` registration and dynamic native-symbol lookup. A library may export only `JNI_OnLoad`; therefore symbol lookup must not assume every Java native method is exported under its mangled name.

## 2. Current MiniAndroid audit required

At the current HEAD, trace this whole chain with exact symbols and source lines:

1. APK scan: identify `lib/<abi>/*.so` entries and record ELF class, machine, dependencies, and hashes.
2. ABI decision: select only a native ABI actually executable in the current runtime/host configuration. The project prioritizes x86/x86_64 native APKs. Do not treat ARM/ARM64-only packages as normal-wave runtime failures.
3. Install identity: extract/copy selected libraries into the installed package's real native library directory; verify bytes and preserve package boundaries.
4. `System.loadLibrary` / `System.load` dispatch through the real DEX call path.
5. Name-to-path resolution and dependency search, including a useful `dlerror` on failure.
6. ELF loader invocation: decide, with evidence, whether the host `dlopen` approach can execute this ABI and satisfy Android-specific dependencies, or whether a guest ELF/dynamic-linker strategy is required. A 64-bit host cannot simply assume it can `dlopen` a 32-bit x86 library in-process.
7. `JNI_OnLoad` invocation with the runtime's actual VM/JNIEnv contract and validation of its returned JNI version.
8. `RegisterNatives` mapping of class + method name + descriptor to native entry point.
9. Dynamic symbol fallback for methods not registered explicitly.
10. First native method dispatch from DEX, correct return/exception handling, and safe failure when a symbol or dependency is missing.
11. Per-library/per-class-loader identity, repeated load behavior, and package isolation.
12. Native rendering path for one small app/fixture, if its ABI and dependencies are supported.

Separate already implemented pre-native legs from the absent or partial execution leg. Do not label a phantom directory, fake native-method registration, a load probe, or a synthetic success as native execution.

## 3. Smallest useful conformance fixtures

Prefer a tiny x86_64 JNI fixture built from source and packaged as a real APK. Record the toolchain and artifact hashes. Add an x86 32-bit fixture only if the host/runtime can actually execute it; otherwise explicitly classify it as ABI/prerequisite-blocked rather than an engine bug.

Required tests:
- **Basic load:** Java calls `System.loadLibrary("mini_probe")`; the library exports `JNI_OnLoad` and registers one method with `RegisterNatives`; the method returns a unique sentinel value.
- **Dynamic symbol fallback:** a second native method is resolved dynamically if the runtime claims to support that path.
- **Missing library:** expected Android-compatible exception/error, useful path/search diagnostics, no fake success.
- **Missing dependency / wrong ELF machine / wrong ELF class:** reject with a diagnostic that distinguishes the failure type.
- **JNI_OnLoad failure:** wrong/unsupported version or pending failure must prevent successful load/dispatch.
- **Registration failure:** invalid class/method/descriptor must not silently map to an unrelated method.
- **Repeated load:** verify the intended same-loader behavior without rerunning initialization unexpectedly.
- **Isolation:** another package cannot load an app-private library merely by guessing its path.
- **Negative control:** run the same Java call with the library absent and prove it fails rather than invoking a HOST_COMPATIBILITY_STUB.
- **Real-app frontier:** revisit the recorded Asteroids/GodotView first arrest only after the minimal fixture passes. Capture the actual native method and loader trace; do not claim a game fix based solely on the fixture.

Run the minimal fixture three times from fresh runtime state. If a cross-app implementation change is made, run A/B regression on representative pure-Java apps and native-dependent apps.

## 4. Architectural decision must follow evidence

Do not jump directly to a full ELF linker port or assume host `dlopen` is sufficient. Compare at least:
- host `dlopen` for compatible host-native ELF and dependency closure;
- a dedicated guest/native compatibility path if Android ELF/linker namespaces or ABI mismatch make host loading invalid;
- explicit capability boundary for unsupported ABI/Android-native dependencies.

For each option, report ABI compatibility, dependency resolution, symbol resolution, JNI semantics, security/isolation, build complexity, memory impact, and app-family fan-out. Do not change the runtime architecture in this research card without a reproducible test demonstrating the current boundary and a minimal proposal.

## 5. Required evidence and status

Record:
- current tested HEAD and binary SHA;
- source SHAs and exact source symbols;
- APK and each `.so` SHA, ELF class/machine, selected ABI;
- extraction destination and byte hash;
- exact load call, `dlerror`, `JNI_OnLoad` result, registration table, and native invocation result;
- expected/actual values, command, exit code, logs and evidence paths;
- positive and negative controls and three-run result;
- cross-app regression outcome;
- tests not run and ABI/dependency prerequisites.

Use statuses precisely:
- `SOURCE_FOUND` for inspected source only;
- `IMPLEMENTED` for code landed;
- `TESTED` for named deterministic tests;
- `OBSERVED` for real-app runtime evidence;
- `PARTIAL` where only some legs work;
- `BLOCKED` for a real missing prerequisite;
- `PENDING` where no evidence exists yet.

## 6. Return result in this same Issue #364

Update the existing UPP-001/native root rather than creating a duplicate. Include a concise ledger with each stage (APK scan, ABI select, extraction, load, ELF/linker, JNI_OnLoad, RegisterNatives, native call, negative controls, real-app frontier), its status, tested HEAD, evidence link, and remaining gap.

Explicitly state what was already proven before this card and what new test was actually run. If only source review was possible, say so and leave execution pending.

**Goal:** establish the smallest reusable native-loading/JNI contract that can unlock entire x86/x86_64 app/game families—not merely make a native library path look real.

# RESEARCH ADDENDUM — MG-150 / MG-147: TRANSFORMED TOUCH HIT-TESTING + POINTER ROUTING (SOURCE-BACKED CANDIDATE)

This is a researcher finding, not a claim that MiniAndroid has a confirmed runtime bug. I inspected the current default-branch `docs/MICRO_GAP_REGISTRY.json` (blob SHA `b84aa999f767cc077cea897f49b50d3a8e638c10`): MG-150 is `PARTIAL` (“translation properties implemented; hit-test interaction with transforms fenced by G06 only”), and MG-147 is `PARTIAL` (“multiple pointer IDs” implemented but not individually fenced). Their recorded upstream source is View/ViewGroup. This is a precise candidate cluster; first reconcile those rows against the current HEAD and existing #288/G06 evidence before editing.

## External answer — exact upstream mechanism

AOSP ViewGroup source:
- https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/master/core/java/android/view/ViewGroup.java
- Exact symbols: `dispatchTouchEvent`, `dispatchTransformedTouchEvent`, `getTransformedMotionEvent`, `transformPointToViewLocal`.
- The current source transforms parent-space coordinates into child-local coordinates by subtracting the child’s layout offset (accounting for parent scroll), then applying the child’s inverse matrix when the child is translated/scaled/rotated. The transformed event is dispatched to the child; temporary event copies are recycled and mutable event action/coordinates are restored. The dispatch path also intersects pointer-ID bitsets, splits events when only a subset of pointers belongs to a child, and avoids dispatching a non-CANCEL event with zero relevant pointers.

The critical law is not “subtract translationX/Y from x/y.” It is **hit-test and dispatch in the same coordinate space, using the inverse of the full child transform**, while preserving pointer IDs, action semantics, and the original event for sibling/parent dispatch.

## Local comparison and hypothesis

Registry evidence says MG-150 is only fenced by G06 for transform basics, while the interaction between transformed hit-testing and event delivery remains explicitly incomplete/unfenced. This establishes a test gap, not a proven bug. Do not assume current code is wrong: trace the actual MiniAndroid path first and classify it as `ALREADY_FIXED`, `TEST_GAP`, `CONFIRMED_BUG`, `DUPLICATE`, or `BLOCKED`.

Inspect the real ViewGroup/View input implementation and identify:
1. Which coordinate space is used for the child hit rectangle.
2. Whether parent scroll and child left/top offsets are applied exactly once.
3. Whether the inverse full transform (not just translation) is applied consistently to hit-testing and delivered MotionEvent coordinates.
4. Whether transformed bounds and hit geometry agree for scale/rotation/negative translation.
5. Whether pointer IDs remain stable when pointer index/order changes.
6. Whether POINTER_DOWN/POINTER_UP splitting and ACTION_CANCEL are correct.
7. Whether the original MotionEvent is restored after dispatch and temporary copies are recycled.
8. Whether the parent intercept path can cancel a child that previously owned the gesture.

## Minimal algorithm to compare against (not blind-patch instructions)

For each candidate child, in order:
- Convert the incoming point from parent coordinates to child-local coordinates: parent scroll offset minus child layout origin, then apply the inverse child matrix when non-identity.
- Test the point against the child’s local hit bounds (and the project’s documented touch-slop policy, if present).
- For dispatch, create/obtain a transformed MotionEvent when matrix transformation or pointer filtering requires it; transform every pointer’s coordinates consistently, not only pointer index 0.
- Intersect incoming pointer IDs with the child’s owned pointer-ID set. If filtering changes the set, use a split event and preserve the correct action/index mapping.
- Deliver CANCEL when ownership is revoked; never synthesize a normal pointer event with zero pointers.
- Restore mutable event state and recycle only the temporary event in a guaranteed cleanup path.

Do not paste this pseudocode into production before comparing with the current implementation; reuse the existing event and matrix abstractions rather than introducing a second coordinate-transform implementation.

## Required falsifiable probe

Add a named law test using a real ViewGroup → child hierarchy and real MotionEvent objects (DEX fixture where the current harness permits):
- Baseline child at (20,30), known size; tap a point inside and a point just outside.
- Repeat after translationX/Y, non-unit scale, rotation, and parent scroll.
- Verify hit-test ownership and child-local event coordinates against a small independent inverse-matrix oracle.
- Use two pointers with non-consecutive IDs; change pointer index/order and verify IDs and action semantics remain stable.
- Exercise POINTER_DOWN, POINTER_UP, parent interception and ACTION_CANCEL.
- Negative controls: an untransformed sibling at the same visual area must not steal the event; a point outside the transformed hit region must not be delivered.
- Verify the original event’s action/coordinates are unchanged after dispatch.
- Run three fresh executions, capture trace/state assertions and add the test to the canonical battery.

## Fan-out and regression

This is potentially shared by buttons, custom Views, drag/gesture controls, scrollable containers, games, transformed animations and nested layouts. Prove actual fan-out by selecting two independent existing x86/x86_64-compatible corpus targets that exercise the changed path; do not infer benefit from a passing synthetic fixture alone. Re-run G06 and the relevant input/lifecycle/render batteries, with exact before/after deltas.

## Evidence to return here

Use the mandatory #364 result schema: current remote HEAD and binary SHA; local file:function:line; upstream URL + exact symbols; match classification; first divergence; fixture and negative control; three-run IDs/hashes; at least two independent targets or an explicit blocker; regression deltas; registry/worklog changes; and remaining uncertainty.

**No new root ID yet.** Reuse MG-150/MG-147 unless the trace proves a distinct first divergence. This addendum is source-backed research and a testable solution path; it does not mark the local defect as confirmed or implemented.

# FOUNDATION 6/4 — TURN HOURS/DAYS OF DEBUGGING INTO A 1–2 MINUTE FIRST-DIVERGENCE TEST

## Objective (measurable)
For a known runtime contract, the normal inner loop must be: run one named probe → see the first violated semantic edge + minimal trace → change code → rerun in ~1–2 minutes. The full battery remains mandatory before accepting a change; it must not be the first diagnostic tool for every small hypothesis.

## What I verified in the repository
- Current test entry point is `scripts/test/run_test_battery.sh`. It rebuilds and runs a broad set of stages; it already has same-HEAD resume checkpoints, but this is a regression gate, not a convenient one-contract diagnostic.
- The existing source-mining report `docs/UPSTREAM_SOURCE_MINING_REPORT.md` says only 7 of the intended 30–50 upstream candidates were deeply audited in CONT-71. That is a second time sink: source discovery, semantic probes and evidence recording need a repeatable format.
- Existing #364 contract already requires source-first, positive/negative controls, first divergence, three-run proof for acceptance, and no false PASS. This card operationalizes that contract; it does not replace it.
- Reference model: Robolectric documents that many Android framework classes run as real Java implementations in a JVM, while instrumentation/shadows are used for platform/native boundaries; its tests can run in seconds. Use it as a source/test-design reference only—not as a new runtime dependency or as proof that MiniAndroid behaves correctly. Sources: https://robolectric.org/architecture/ and https://robolectric.org/

## Proposed reusable solution — a fast probe tier, not weaker acceptance criteria

Add a thin, deterministic runner around the EXISTING test/fixture infrastructure (first inspect and reuse existing builders; do not create a competing harness):

1. `scripts/test/run_semantic_probe.sh --root MG-116 --case invalidate_child`
   - Resolves the root/case to a checked-in manifest entry.
   - Verifies HEAD, worktree status, fixture/source hashes and binary build identity.
   - Rebuilds only if the relevant binary is stale; compiles the tiny fixture once and caches it by fixture-source SHA + compiler/toolchain identity.
   - Executes only the named probe and its positive/negative controls; never silently skips a missing case.
   - Prints the earliest failed edge, expected vs actual value, and a compact causal trace. Exit 0 only if every required row ran and passed; missing evidence is BLOCKED/FAIL, not PASS.
   - Emits machine-readable JSONL with HEAD, binary SHA256, command, test ID, expected/actual, trace path, output SHA, duration, and status.

2. Keep three explicit tiers:
   - **T0 semantic probe (target 1–2 min):** one law, tiny fixture, deterministic inputs; no full APK corpus.
   - **T1 root/fan-out regression (few representative independent families):** run only after T0 passes.
   - **T2 full battery / three fresh runs / screenshots and corpus gates:** required for accepting a runtime change, not required for each exploratory edit.

3. Use a shared probe contract so the runner can report the first divergence consistently:
   `SETUP → INPUT → EXPECTED LAW → OBSERVED VALUE → FIRST DIVERGENCE → NEGATIVE CONTROL → RESULT`.
   Each probe must assert observable semantics—not merely method invocation, process exit, a non-empty trace or PNG existence. Cache fixture compilation, not correctness results across changed source/binary. Same-HEAD resume is allowed only when the runner proves the exact source, binary and fixture identities match.

## Concrete first pilot: existing MG-116 View invalidation root
Existing record says MG-116 is PARTIAL because dedicated law tests are pending. Do not presume the runtime implementation is broken; make the test decide.

Use the actual MiniAndroid framework/DEX fixture and the existing render/frame-pump path:
- Baseline: child View paints region A; capture app-owned draw count, measure/layout counters, root traversal markers and output pixel/hash.
- Action: mutate only child state A→B, call `invalidate()` (not `requestLayout()`).
- Positive assertion: a later traversal reaches the child draw and final app-owned pixels change A→B.
- Negative assertions: measure/layout counters do not increment solely due to invalidate; no unrelated root/view receives a fabricated draw.
- Propagation variant: nested child invalidation must reach the root; repeated invalidations may coalesce but may not lose the pending traversal.
- Negative control: without the state mutation/invalidate, the image and counters remain stable.
- Report the first failed edge among child dirty state → parent propagation → root pending traversal → traversal execution → app-owned draw → final pixels. Do not fix anything until this probe identifies which edge actually fails.

Upstream contract sources already known:
- AOSP View invalidation: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/master/core/java/android/view/View.java
- AOSP ViewGroup descendant propagation: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/master/core/java/android/view/ViewGroup.java
- AOSP ViewRootImpl traversal scheduling: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/android12-release/core/java/android/view/ViewRootImpl.java

## Reusable source-to-probe card for every next root
For each selected upstream method/test, record: upstream URL + pinned revision + exact symbol; local file/function; semantic law in one sentence; fixture input; expected output; negative control; first-divergence trace point; affected independent families; existing root/issue IDs; runtime to run; and remaining uncertainty. A source link alone is SOURCE_FOUND, not a reproduced bug.

## Guardrails
- No new issue for a root already tracked; report progress here in #364 and update its canonical registry/worklog.
- Do not import Robolectric wholesale or treat its shadows as the answer. Translate the semantic law into a MiniAndroid-native probe.
- Do not relax the existing full-battery/three-run acceptance bar. Fast T0 shortens diagnosis; T2 still protects compatibility.
- Do not add package-specific fixes, forced redraw/pixels, arbitrary polling, or cached PASS results whose source/binary identity differs.
- The first delivery should include the exact runner diff, one passing and one intentionally failing fixture proving the diagnostic catches the violation, measured cold/warm runtimes, and evidence that a changed source invalidates the cache.

## Success criterion
A coder can select an existing root ID and run one command to get a trustworthy first-divergence answer in ≤120 seconds on the normal CPU/headless environment. If this target is not met, report the measured bottleneck (build, fixture compilation, APK startup, frame pump, or evidence capture) and optimize that bottleneck—not by weakening the test.

# FOUNDATION 7/4 — UNREGISTERED STORAGE-SANDBOX ESCAPE CANDIDATE (SOURCE-VERIFIED, RUNTIME NOT YET REPRODUCED)

## Why I am flagging this separately
I compared the current default-branch `docs/MICRO_GAP_REGISTRY.json`, `docs/LOAD_COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX.jsonl`, and the actual `miniandroid/src/storage/data_root.cpp` source. The registry has many storage/API rows, but I did not find a dedicated canonical micro-gap row for path containment / cross-package authorization. The old compatibility matrix does mention `'..' unguarded`, but that matrix is dated to older code and must not be accepted as proof by itself. This card therefore treats the current source as a concrete test candidate, not a claimed runtime exploit or a new duplicate implementation ticket.

This is related to the P0-A concern in FOUNDATION 3/4 (comment 6202665605); reuse that root if the coder has already registered it elsewhere. The specific missing fence here is a compact adversarial path-containment suite and a canonical current status.

## Current local source — exact risky branches
File: https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/blob/main/miniandroid/src/storage/data_root.cpp

1. `Storage::resolve_android_path()` relative branch:
```cpp
if (logical[0] != '/') {
    r.category = PathCategory::RELATIVE_APP_DATA;
    r.host_path = package_data_dir() / logical;
    r.allowed = true;
    return r;
}
```
No lexical/canonical containment check is performed before `allowed=true`. Inputs such as `../../other-package/shared_prefs/Prefs.xml` can syntactically escape the package root after filesystem path resolution.

2. Absolute `/data/data/<pkg>/...` branch extracts any package string containing a dot and maps it to that package's backing directory; it does not compare `pkg` with `g_context_package` or a permission/grant decision before returning `allowed=true`.

3. `/data/user/<id>/<pkg>/...` and `/data/user_de/<id>/<pkg>/...` similarly accept any dotted package name without checking the active caller identity.

4. External volume dispatch uses `logical.rfind("/storage/emulated/0", 0) == 0`, so the mount prefix is tested without a path-component boundary. Strings such as `/storage/emulated/0evil/...` enter the virtual external branch. This may be a separate low-cost edge, but keep it in the same containment probe family until proven to need a separate root.

5. The system-font mapping also appends the caller tail under `<root>/system/fonts` without an explicit canonical containment check; e.g. a tail containing `../../` deserves a negative-control test.

## External semantic/security references already found
- Android Developers, “Path traversal”: https://developer.android.com/privacy-and-security/risks/path-traversal?hl=en
  The documented risk is user-controlled path components such as `../` escaping the intended directory; mitigation is canonicalizing and checking the result against the expected directory.
- Android app-specific storage contract: https://developer.android.com/training/data-storage/app-specific
  Internal app data is intended to be private to that app; the OS prevents other apps from accessing it.
- This is not merely an API fidelity detail. If multiple packages share one host process and storage root, the runtime must enforce the isolation that Android normally provides through UID/filesystem policy.

## Minimal fast probe — no APK corpus needed
Build a tiny direct test for `resolve_android_path()` using a temporary data root and bind context package `org.example.alpha`. Create sentinel files under alpha, beta, the virtual mount and the virtual system-font root. Assert both the returned `allowed/category/host_path` and actual read/write behavior.

Required cases:
- PASS: `files/ok.txt` resolves inside alpha's package data root.
- DENY: `../../data/data/org.example.beta/shared_prefs/secret.xml` cannot escape alpha's root.
- DENY unless an explicit supported grant exists: `/data/data/org.example.beta/shared_prefs/secret.xml` from alpha.
- DENY or policy-defined: `/data/user/0/org.example.beta/...` and `/data/user_de/0/org.example.beta/...` from alpha.
- DENY: `/storage/emulated/0evil/secret` must not be treated as a child of the mount.
- DENY: `/system/fonts/../../data/data/org.example.beta/...` must not escape the virtual system-font subtree.
- POSITIVE CONTROL: legitimate same-package `/data/data/org.example.alpha/files/ok.txt` and the documented `/data/user/0/org.example.alpha` alias still resolve correctly.
- Isolation control: switching the bound context to beta must not make alpha's private files readable unless a separately specified Android API/permission permits it.

Use both lexical traversal and symlink/canonical escape cases if the host filesystem allows symlinks. The containment check must be applied consistently at the shared resolver boundary, but do not blindly reject legitimate Android aliases, device nodes, installed-APK paths, or shared-storage paths. Preserve the existing intentional deviations and define allowed categories explicitly.

## Correct fix shape if the probe reproduces the issue
Normalize and validate the resolved host path against the allowed canonical root for its category; enforce package identity for private CE/DE storage; use component-boundary prefix checks rather than raw string prefixes. Avoid checking only for the literal substring `..`: canonicalization and containment must cover equivalent paths and symlinks. Keep the policy centralized so BitmapFactory, File, streams, SQLite and asset consumers cannot each implement a different sandbox.

## Required proof and classification
- First fetch current HEAD, worktree and canonical registry/root IDs. If this is already implemented or already tracked, report ALREADY_FIXED/DUPLICATE and link the exact root; do not create another ID.
- First run the direct resolver probe, positive + negative controls, before any fix.
- If reproduced, add a named fast test to the existing battery and capture exact host paths/allowed flags; then run relevant file/stream/SQLite/Bitmap consumers and at least one independent APK family.
- Keep this labelled SOURCE_FOUND/OBSERVED/REPRODUCED/ROOT-CAUSED separately. This card currently claims only SOURCE_FOUND + code-path risk; no runtime reproduction has been performed by the researcher.
- Update the existing registry and worklog with current evidence; do not trust stale `LOAD_COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX.jsonl` status without reconciling it to the current HEAD.

## Why this is high-fan-out
A single resolver is shared by many storage consumers. A central containment/identity fix plus a sub-minute deterministic probe can prevent cross-package data bleed and remove repeated per-consumer debugging. This is a foundational correctness/isolation contract, not an app-specific symptom.

# FOUNDATION 8/4 — 2D GAME “LOADS BUT ISN'T COMPLETE” FORENSIC WAVE (ROOT-FIRST, NO APP HACKS)

## What I checked before choosing this wave
I re-read the current default-branch game evidence and micro-gap registry, rather than selecting another generic renderer rewrite.

Primary records:
- `docs/VERIFIED_EXECUTED_GAMES.md` (current file SHA `e354f30a2ac62990e3ce21bc5d53373366b9911c`)
- `docs/EXECUTED_GIFS.md` (SHA `b69db45d7811c2f6c356a9558338f3957552ba0b`)
- `docs/MICRO_GAP_REGISTRY.json` (SHA `b84aa999f767cc077cea897f49b50d3a8e638c10`)
- `docs/LOAD_COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX.jsonl` (SHA `4da20e4af085d60ad512b19dd85d355087ee702a`)
- Existing #364 foundations 1–7, especially classic View invalidation (comment 6201554037), Compose wake-up (6201700020), and the transformed-touch addendum (6207963395).

This wave targets real 2D game cases that are already beyond the “blank screen / process launched” stage but remain visually partial or have incomplete semantic proof. Do not downgrade these to a generic “Canvas missing” hypothesis: the repo already has broad Canvas law tests, so the next step is to identify the first divergence on the real game path.

## Evidence-backed target shortlist (not all are the same root)
1. **Vector Pinball / Bouncy — `com.dozingcatsoftware.bouncy`**: current game evidence says the run is visually partial; S95 noted 3x WRONG_COLOR cleared but 1 clip residual. It is a useful first raster/clip target because the game has a small frame set and a known visual residual. Inspect its exact canonical screenshot and S95 evidence before changing code.
2. **Snake Deluxe — `com.miniandroid.snakedeluxe`**: real gameplay and restart/state change are proven, but the game record explicitly says rendering L3 struct-candidate and the graphics verdict is not SEMANTIC_PASS. This is a useful first-divergence target because the gameplay sequence exists; do not re-debug input unless current trace says input is the first failure.
3. **Mini Tetris — `com.miniandroid.tetris`**: 6 unique frames per 24-frame run are deterministic, but the record is still VISUALLY_PARTIAL. This separates deterministic state progression from complete visual correctness.
4. **2048 — `com.miniandroid.g2048`**: score/tile changes are proven over 65 frames, while the record notes rendering L2 and an unpromoted human-review gate. Verify whether its remaining deficit is visual output, test/verdict classification, or both.
5. **TicTacToe Classic — `com.emmanuelmess.tictactoe`**: interaction changes are recorded, but graphics verification failed and the status is PARTIAL. It is a compact control case to compare app-owned pixel provenance against actual game state.
6. **Dooz / BlockBlast** are a separate Compose family, not to be folded into the 2D View/Canvas root. Current #364 comment 6201700020 already splits their Compose fronts; resume it only if the requested game wave demonstrates the failure is actually on the Compose path.

The evidence above proves these are good forensic targets; it does NOT prove they share one defect.

## New actionable discovery: the game loop can be “alive” while its render clock is not
The current registry has a specific under-fenced combination:
- MG-223 ValueAnimator basic timing is marked CLOSED, but its own note explicitly says animator-driving Choreographer integration remains future work and animators do not yet tick the render clock.
- MG-228 wrong-order frame detection is PARTIAL; dedicated fixtures are pending.
- MG-229 disappearing-object detection is PARTIAL; dedicated fixtures are pending.
- MG-116 invalidate propagation is PARTIAL; its dedicated law test/evidence fields are empty.
- MG-221/222/224/225/226 are only OBSERVED from selected games; observation of a few gameplay sequences is not a generic timing/frame contract.

Do NOT reopen MG-223 as “ValueAnimator broken” without checking its existing law. Reuse MG-223/MG-228/MG-229/MG-116 and any existing game roots; create no new root until the first divergence is shown to be distinct.

## External source research — the exact reusable timing law
Android's official game-loop guide:
https://developer.android.com/games/develop/gameloops
It warns that the display owns refresh timing, frames may be dropped/repeated, and simulation should advance from elapsed time rather than assuming a fixed number of frames. For SurfaceView/GLSurfaceView-style games, rendering belongs on a dedicated render thread rather than expensive UI-thread work.

libGDX lifecycle:
https://libgdx.com/wiki/app/the-life-cycle
Its contract separates create/resize/render/pause/resume/dispose; render is the recurring game-loop callback.

libGDX threading:
https://libgdx.com/wiki/app/threading
It states ApplicationListener callbacks run on the rendering thread and GL operations must occur there; work submitted from other threads is marshalled to the render thread.

libGDX non-continuous rendering:
https://libgdx.com/wiki/graphics/continuous-and-non-continuous-rendering
This gives an especially useful falsifiable rule: when continuous rendering is disabled, a new frame is requested by input, requestRendering(), or posted render-thread work. A dirty/idle frame pump must not mistake “no immediate runnable” for permanent quiescence if valid future-due work is pending.

Android's hardware-accelerated View drawing model:
https://developer.android.com/topic/performance/views/hardware-accel-views
The draw pipeline has distinct invalidation, display-list recording, and display-list drawing stages. Therefore, a Java draw invocation, a recorded Canvas command, and final pixels are three different proof points.

## Proposed minimal diagnostic algorithm (use existing tracing and fixture tools)
For one target per distinct suspected family, capture one bounded deterministic timeline with monotonically increasing event IDs:
1. input/state mutation or animation tick;
2. Handler/Looper/Choreographer enqueue (due time + callback type);
3. dequeue/execute (or explicit “not due yet”);
4. invalidate/requestRender/Surface callback;
5. root traversal or render-thread frame start;
6. app-owned draw callback/Canvas op summary;
7. raster result: expected region, color histogram, changed-pixel bounding box;
8. final screenshot/presentation result.

At each edge record the expected and observed transition. Stop at the first missing/wrong edge. Do not add arbitrary polling, force every frame, or “fix” the screenshot with a synthetic overlay.

## First probes, ordered by diagnostic value
A. **Frame-clock vs state progression (MG-223/228/229):** a synthetic 2D scene moves one colored sprite A→B→C at known elapsed times. Assert the sequence order, timing tolerance, no disappearing sprite, and stable final frame after stop. Add a negative control with no pending tick and a paused control.
B. **View invalidation vs actual pixels (MG-116):** change only a child Canvas scene's state and invalidate; prove draw callback, app-owned pixel change, and no measure/layout unless requested.
C. **Clip/save/restore and draw order:** use Bouncy's exact failing region as a minimized fixture. Compare app draw trace, clip stack, raster pixel mask and final capture; do not infer a clip bug solely from a wrong screenshot.
D. **Real game trace:** repeat the first failing probe against one target APK from the current corpus. Keep the x86/x86_64 ABI prerequisite check; ARM-only titles are not ordinary runtime failures.
E. **Input only if first divergence:** use the already-open MG-150/MG-147 transformed hit-test investigation if transformed/scroll coordinates are the first broken edge. Do not re-run all input tests when the game state already changes correctly.

## Required outcome in this same issue
Return a small table for each target: current HEAD + binary SHA; ABI; launch/content evidence; state-change evidence; expected visual region; first divergence; root ID reused; whether the defect is runtime, incomplete test, or verdict drift; exact local function and upstream symbol; minimal test; positive/negative controls; cold/warm runtime; screenshot/pixel hashes; independent second-family fan-out; regressions.

The initial fast probe should take ≤120 seconds after the binary/fixture is warm. Full corpus gates remain mandatory after a fix. Do not count a deterministic GIF, nonzero draw-op count, process exit, or a screenshot file alone as proof of full rendering.

## Explicit stop rule
If the first divergence is in the common frame clock, invalidate propagation, clipping/raster, or provenance chain, fix/test that generic law and replay at least two independent 2D games. If it is only one game's asset/layout/animation code, first prove whether an Android API contract is missing; no package-name branches or app-specific pixel patches. If the visual verifier itself is wrong, fix the verifier separately and preserve the runtime verdict until re-measured.

# FOUNDATION 9/4 — NEW HIGH-SEVERITY BLANK/INCOMPLETE 2D GAME CLASS: LIBGDX NATIVE BOOTSTRAP + SMALL-APK TRIAGE

## Why this is a new investigation (not another GIF review)
I re-read the current `docs/LOAD_COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX.jsonl` and `docs/VERIFIED_EXECUTED_GAMES.md`. The matrix explicitly labels `native_libs` as MISSING: `System.loadLibrary` unhandled, no .so extraction, JNI is mostly stubs, and `nativeLibraryDir` is phantom. It separately labels the provider initialization stage MISSING and the resources/image path BROKEN/PARTIAL. This is a much more severe, source-predictable blocker for an entire family of games than another visual mismatch in a game already producing GIFs.

Current source-of-truth to reconcile before acting:
- `docs/LOAD_COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX.jsonl` blob `4da20e4af085d60ad512b19dd85d355087ee702a`
- `docs/VERIFIED_EXECUTED_GAMES.md` blob `e354f30a2ac62990e3ce21bc5d53373366b9911c`
- `docs/MICRO_GAP_REGISTRY.json` blob `b84aa999f767cc077cea897f49b50d3a8e638c10`
The game audit also says 64 titles have trace-only E3 evidence with no meaningful visual; do not treat these as “executed games” or start with the already-GIF-verified set.

## Upstream game source chosen for source-first analysis
A compact, inspectable Android 2D sample is `jmillikan/gdx-tetris`, whose README explicitly describes it as a simple libGDX block-dropping game targeted at Android:
https://github.com/jmillikan/gdx-tetris
Android module: https://github.com/jmillikan/gdx-tetris/tree/master/gdx-tetris-android
Core game source: https://github.com/jmillikan/gdx-tetris/tree/master/gdx-tetris

This is an upstream source exemplar, NOT yet a claim that its APK is in our corpus or ABI-compatible. The coder must inspect its actual Android launcher, dependencies, assets, and generated APK ABI. Do not spend the wave building a modern source project if a small existing corpus APK exercises the same contract.

## Exact source-level boot contract
In upstream libGDX:
- `AndroidApplication.initialize(...)` calls `config.nativeLoader.load()` before it creates the graphics/input/audio objects and installs the view:
  https://github.com/libgdx/libgdx/blob/master/backends/gdx-backend-android/src/com/badlogic/gdx/backends/android/AndroidApplication.java
- `GdxNativesLoader.load()` calls `new SharedLibraryLoader().load("gdx")`:
  https://github.com/libgdx/libgdx/blob/master/gdx/src/com/badlogic/gdx/utils/GdxNativesLoader.java
- A normal libGDX 2D path uses OpenGL-backed graphics objects such as `SpriteBatch`/Texture/Mesh, not Android View Canvas:
  https://github.com/libgdx/libgdx/blob/master/gdx/src/com/badlogic/gdx/graphics/g2d/SpriteBatch.java

This gives a falsifiable hypothesis: if a candidate app reaches libGDX initialization but MiniAndroid cannot resolve/load the ABI-matching `gdx` native library (or cannot create its GLES-backed surface/context), it may fail before the first meaningful game frame. A blank screen alone does NOT identify which of those edges is broken. First-divergence evidence must distinguish JNI/native load, Activity/view attach, surface creation, GL context, ApplicationListener.create(), and first render.

## Task A — source audit and pick three small candidates (coder performs all APK tests)
1. Fetch/reconcile current HEAD, build SHA, worktree, ABI inventory and game evidence first.
2. Search the existing corpus for games with no meaningful screenshot / E3 trace-only / blank or partial output. Choose three small APKs (prefer low APK size) from distinct families where available:
   - one libGDX / JNI-backed 2D game,
   - one pure Java/Kotlin Canvas/View 2D game,
   - one SurfaceView/GLSurfaceView or other native-backed 2D game.
3. Enforce the project's normal ABI rule before testing: APK must include executable x86 or x86_64 native code if it needs native code. ARM-only APK is a prerequisite mismatch, not a MiniAndroid runtime failure. Record APK SHA256, package, version, minSdk, ABI list, native .so names/ELF machine, and APK size.
4. For each candidate, inspect the source (or decompile only when source is unavailable) from manifest/launcher through initialization and first draw. Identify the earliest API/library contract that must work before the first real frame.
5. Run the exact same APK on MiniAndroid with a bounded 120-second probe. Collect first-divergence trace, exception/Logcat, lifecycle, view tree, surface/GL state, draw count, app-owned pixel region, screenshot SHA and whether the first meaningful frame ever appeared. Do not merely report launch success or a GIF.

## Task B — minimal generic probes before changing runtime
Create/reuse fast probes for these distinct edges:
- NATIVE_LOAD: loadLibrary("gdx") resolves only a matching ABI library, maps its dependencies and reports a real error on missing/incompatible ELF; never mark a phantom path as loaded.
- ACTIVITY_VIEW: initializeForView/initialize installs and attaches the returned view, and lifecycle callback ordering is observed.
- SURFACE_GL: surface-created callback precedes GL-dependent create/render; context currentness and GL errors are observable.
- FIRST_FRAME: one known clear-color/triangle-or-texture draw reaches app-owned pixels; distinguish GL command submission from actual raster/presentation.
- ASSET: the game can open a known packaged asset through the correct libGDX file type; no fake default texture or blank fallback may count as success.
Use positive and negative controls. If the candidate is pure Canvas and has no native/GL path, do not force it through the libGDX hypothesis; use its actual first divergence.

## Task C — likely generic fix shape if native load is the reproduced first divergence
Do not patch package names. Complete the shared native contract:
- APK ABI-aware extraction/resolution into a real per-package nativeLibraryDir;
- verify ELF class/machine and required dependencies before load;
- implement the supported System.loadLibrary/System.load path and explicit unsupported/error behavior for unavailable symbols;
- JNI_OnLoad/RegisterNatives/dynamic-symbol resolution only to the degree demanded by the chosen small candidates;
- record requested library, resolved path, ABI, ELF machine, dependency failures and exact result in the runtime trace.
Do not pretend JNI stubs are native execution. If native load succeeds but surface/context creation fails, fix the actual surface/GL boundary instead; these are separate roots.

## Task D — second source family and real solution
For each of the three candidate game sources, report:
- launch Activity/entry class and first application callback;
- exact methods called before first frame;
- upstream source URL + pinned commit/revision + symbol;
- local MiniAndroid file/function implementing that contract;
- first missing semantic edge, expected vs observed;
- proposed minimal source diff (or exact pseudocode referencing local functions) and the smallest fixture that fails before/pass after;
- ABI and source licensing/provenance.
Then test only after the researcher/coder has a root-backed patch. Replay the same APK and one independent APK from the same API family. If the source predicts a contract absent in the runtime, add a deterministic probe even if the APK happens to work by a fallback path.

## Acceptance/evidence contract
- Do not add a new GitHub issue; this is a continuation of #364 and must reuse UPP-001/native/JNI, provider, Surface/GL or graphics roots if they already exist.
- Do not use any of the six previously GIF-reviewed games as the primary discovery target.
- Do not infer a shared root from three blank screens; report independent first divergences.
- No APK parse, method-call log, non-zero draw count, process survival, or screenshot-file existence alone counts as meaningful rendering.
- At least one intentionally failing fixture and one passing control for the chosen first-divergence law; record cold/warm runtimes.
- Final result must state which candidates were actually tested, which were blocked by ABI/prerequisites, which root was reproduced, the exact code diff, and cross-family regression. If no x86/x86_64 candidate exists in the local corpus, report that fact and use a tiny purpose-built x86_64 fixture; do not silently switch to ARM-only.
- Do not claim the researcher has run the APK tests: these are explicitly assigned to the coder. The current result is source-audited hypothesis + reproducible test plan, not a runtime finding.

## Expected value
This should expose an unregistered “fails before first frame” root with high fan-out, or decisively falsify the native-load hypothesis and move to the true first divergence. Either outcome is better than reviewing more already-working GIFs.
