# FOUNDATION 10/4 — SPECIFIC GAME/FAMILY, ROOT, AND MY PROPOSED BASE FIX

## Target game and problem
Source exemplar: `jmillikan/gdx-tetris`, a small Android/libGDX 2D game:
- https://github.com/jmillikan/gdx-tetris
- Android launcher: https://github.com/jmillikan/gdx-tetris/tree/master/gdx-tetris-android
- Game logic: https://github.com/jmillikan/gdx-tetris/tree/master/gdx-tetris

This is an upstream source exemplar, not yet confirmed as an APK in our corpus. Coder must find the smallest matching x86/x86_64 native-compatible game in the corpus; ARM-only is a prerequisite mismatch, not a runtime bug.

**Problem hypothesis:** a libGDX game may fail before its first real frame because its Android bootstrap requires native-library loading and then a functioning graphics backend. MiniAndroid's current matrix labels native libraries missing, `System.loadLibrary` unhandled, `nativeLibraryDir` phantom, and JNI mostly stubs. The current `miniandroid/src/jni/jni_bridge.h` (blob `52bc2c4c784ff209099558d2f5f40cdf3b01ac1e`) even contains a “NativeLoader.init(...) — stub success” log path. This is a concrete source/runtime contract mismatch to test, not yet proof that a particular APK fails for this reason.

## Source proof
1. libGDX `AndroidApplication.init(...)` calls `config.nativeLoader.load()` before creating graphics/input/audio/files:
https://github.com/libgdx/libgdx/blob/master/backends/gdx-backend-android/src/com/badlogic/gdx/backends/android/AndroidApplication.java
2. `GdxNativesLoader.load()` delegates to the shared-library loader:
https://github.com/libgdx/libgdx/blob/master/gdx/src/com/badlogic/gdx/utils/GdxNativesLoader.java
3. Application startup depends on the backend calling the ApplicationListener lifecycle/render path:
https://github.com/libgdx/libgdx/blob/master/gdx/src/com/badlogic/gdx/Application.java
4. Local matrix: `docs/LOAD_COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX.jsonl`, blob `4da20e4af085d60ad512b19dd85d355087ee702a`, row `native_libs` says System.loadLibrary unhandled, no .so extraction, phantom nativeLibraryDir, JNI mostly stubs. Reuse existing UPP-001 / FOUNDATION 5/4; no duplicate root.

## My proposed base fix
Do not claim native loading succeeded unless a real compatible library was resolved and validated.

- Resolve `System.loadLibrary(name)` to `lib{name}.so` from the installed package's ABI inventory; no package-name or hard-coded-path special cases.
- Validate ELF class/machine and dependencies against the executable runtime ABI before loading. Extract only the matching ABI library to the real per-package nativeLibraryDir.
- Make `System.loadLibrary` and `System.load` use the same resolver and package/class-loader identity rules.
- Record explicit states: REQUESTED → RESOLVED → ABI_VALIDATED → LOADED → JNI_REGISTERED. A registry handler match or log line must never imply LOADED.
- Missing/incompatible libraries must raise an observable Java-visible failure, not return a plausible default.
- Once native loading is proven real, separately trace surface-created → current GL context → ApplicationListener.create() → first render → app-owned pixels. If native load passes, stop blaming the loader and fix the actual first failing edge.

## Coder-only test wave: three small, previously unreviewed APKs
1. Smallest x86/x86_64 libGDX/native 2D game.
2. Smallest pure Java/Kotlin Canvas/View 2D game.
3. Smallest x86/x86_64 SurfaceView/GL/native-backed game, if available.

For each record APK SHA-256, package/version/minSdk, ABI and ELF inventory, launcher, first failed checkpoint, exception/trace, root reused, before/after result and screenshot/pixel hash. Run the named probe within 120 seconds warm where possible. Do not use the six previously GIF-reviewed games as discovery targets.

For the libGDX APK, capture: launcher class initialization; AndroidApplication.init entry; nativeLoader request/result; resolved library path and ELF machine; JNI_OnLoad/RegisterNatives result; graphics/view construction and attachment; surface-created; GL context current; listener create; first render; first app-owned pixels. Stop at the first absent/wrong checkpoint.

## Required controls and decision
- Negative fixture: missing/incompatible ABI library must fail, never log “stub success”.
- Positive fixture: a known-good x86_64 library reaches a real callable native symbol and returns a known value. If this is impossible in the environment, mark BLOCKED/PARTIAL; do not call a stub native execution.
- Pure Canvas positive control and one independent native-backed APK for fan-out.
- Full battery remains mandatory after a real fix.

Coder must return: `APK | ABI | first failed checkpoint | trace/exception | existing root | source symbol | proposed diff | before/after | second-game fan-out`.

Valid outcomes: REPRODUCED + ROOT_CAUSED; FALSIFIED (loader passed); PREREQUISITE_MISMATCH; or BLOCKED with exact evidence. Do not report the libGDX hypothesis as a confirmed cause before the APK tests. The source/runtime contract mismatch is established; the specific runtime failure is not yet established.

# FOUNDATION 11/4 — CONCRETE BLANK GAME SOURCE AUDIT: Memory (eu.quelltext.memory) — WEBVIEW LOCAL-ASSET BOOT + ASYNC SCRIPT RACE

This is the required format: **specific game → source-proven problem → my proposed source/base fix → coder-only APK test**. Do not reuse the previously GIF-reviewed six titles.

## 1) Exact target and current evidence
**Target:** Memory game, package `eu.quelltext.memory`, upstream Android wrapper:
https://github.com/niccokunzmann/app.memory.quelltext.eu
Upstream web game source:
https://github.com/niccokunzmann/memory.quelltext.eu

Current repo evidence in `docs/VERIFIED_EXECUTED_GAMES.md` records Memory as `L0_LOADED_ONLY`, `rendered=false`; the audit explicitly warns that blank-class frames are not visual evidence. This is a genuine not-yet-rendered candidate, not a GIF review.

Upstream source files were fetched and read:
- `app/build.gradle` (blob `e37e3af67f7ca50e22dd4839a6e00be8df31b3ac`): applicationId `eu.quelltext.memory`, version 1.7, minSdk 1, Kotlin, no native dependency listed.
- `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` (blob `6a48af6b1302434ba501bd7b75f11b985d708875`): launcher is `.FullscreenActivity`.
- `app/src/main/java/eu/quelltext/memory/FullscreenActivity.kt` (blob `756789156b85739ccf5ccf14606ef7c1ee327a3f`): `onCreate` inflates `activity_fullscreen`, then calls `web_view.loadUrl("file:///android_asset/memory.quelltext.eu/index.html")`, and only afterwards sets `webSettings.javaScriptEnabled = true`.
- `app/src/main/res/layout/activity_fullscreen.xml` (blob `9295815a18fd1caef957d34e3c89a74589716809`): the entire app content is a match-parent `WebView`.
- `app/src/main/assets/memory.quelltext.eu` is a Git submodule from `https://github.com/niccokunzmann/memory.quelltext.eu.git`; the source's README says it is pure HTML/CSS/JavaScript.
- The HTML `index.html` (blob `c282a9e835f09f0e59873643ab8615593b586ee3`) loads 18 dependent JS files with `async=""`, including compatibility, common, game, state classes, dealers, preload, card, table, pairing, settings and confetti.
- The WebView compatibility matrix row is PARTIAL: QuickJS, `file:///android_asset`, HTTPS and `evaluateJavascript` exist, but `onPageFinished` and `shouldOverrideUrlLoading` are absent, `addJavascriptInterface` is absent, and localStorage has only in-memory storage because `kv_path` is never assigned.

## 2) Two concrete source-level risks — keep them distinct
### Risk A: asynchronous script dependency race (source-proven)
The HTML marks every dependent script `async`. Async scripts have no document-order execution guarantee. But the source has direct dependencies: `game.js` instantiates `InitialState`; `settings.js` constructs/uses `Table`, `dealers`, and `loadAndStartTheGame`; the game requires its state/dealer/card/table code. If the dependent script runs before its definition, the result is a ReferenceError or partially initialized page. This is an upstream application source race, not proof of a MiniAndroid runtime defect.

**My proposed app-source fix for diagnostic A/B only:** change these classic script tags from `async` to `defer` (or remove `async`), preserving their current dependency order; `defer` executes classic scripts in document order after parsing. Do not silently patch the shipped APK or make MiniAndroid globally serialize async scripts. Use a source-built diagnostic APK only if feasible, and record that it is a changed test artifact.

### Risk B: WebView local-asset/document lifecycle gap (base-runtime candidate)
The app's only content surface is WebView, and it immediately loads `file:///android_asset/memory.quelltext.eu/index.html`. MiniAndroid has a QuickJS-backed WebView, but lacks standard navigation/load callbacks and persistent localStorage. The missing callbacks may make the current harness falsely report “loaded” without proving document completion; asset URL resolution or script/CSS/image fetch may also fail silently if missing-asset handling is fake-success. Persistence is unlikely to explain the first blank frame, so do not conflate it with first-render root.

**My proposed base-level fix:** add an observable WebView document-load state machine, not a game-specific branch:
`NAV_REQUESTED → URL_RESOLVED → HTML_BYTES_READ → PARSED → EACH_SCRIPT/STYLE/IMAGE_REQUESTED_AND_RESOLVED → JS_EXECUTED → DOM_READY → LOAD_EVENT → FIRST_NONEMPTY_PAINT`.
Implement real `WebViewClient.onPageFinished` and `shouldOverrideUrlLoading` semantics for supported navigation; log each asset request as success/failure with URL, bytes, MIME type, and owning APK. Resolve relative URLs against the document's `file:///android_asset/...` base, including nested CSS/script/image paths. A missing asset must produce an explicit error, never a fake-success empty body. Do not claim WebView loaded from Activity launch or QuickJS initialization alone.

## 3) Coder-only reproduction plan (≤120 seconds warm)
1. Confirm the local corpus has this APK; record APK SHA256, version, ABI, size, and current binary SHA. If not present, record this and use the smallest existing pure-WebView local-asset APK. No ARM-only native blocker applies if the APK has no native libraries; inspect rather than assume.
2. Run Memory unchanged on MiniAndroid and record the first divergence: Activity onCreate, WebView construction, loadUrl, URL resolver, HTML byte count, parsed script order, first JS exception, DOM/load events, CSS/image requests, and first non-background pixel.
3. Add one synthetic local HTML fixture with two classic scripts A then B where B depends on A, plus one nested CSS background image. Test both `defer`-ordered scripts and intentional async completion permutations. The runtime must preserve browser semantics, not force async order.
4. Negative control: request one nonexistent local asset and require an explicit failed request / WebView error rather than an empty fake success. Positive control: a tiny local page with one heading and one image must produce non-background pixels.
5. If original Memory fails due script race, run a source-built A/B with `async` replaced by `defer`; that is evidence for an app-source defect, not a runtime fix. If script execution is ordered correctly but nested assets or document completion fails, fix the generic WebView/asset contract.
6. Do not touch runtime until the first failing edge is identified. Then test the same base fix on a second independent local-WebView app, with before/after trace, screenshot SHA/pixel-region proof, cold/warm runtime, and regression subset.

## 4) Decision and acceptance
Return:
`APK/SHA | source revision | unchanged or diagnostic build | ABI/native inventory | first failed edge | exact JS/WebView error | app-source race or runtime contract | proposed local diff | before/after result | second-app fan-out`.

Valid outcomes: `APP_SOURCE_RACE`, `RUNTIME_ROOT_REPRODUCED`, `FALSIFIED`, `PREREQUISITE_MISMATCH`, or `BLOCKED` with evidence. Do not call the source race a MiniAndroid bug. Reuse the existing WebView and asset roots; no new issue, no package-name branch, and no completion claim until the coder runs the APK.

# FOUNDATION 12/4 — BALL2BOX (GODOT 3.x) IS L0/BLANK: SOURCE-PROVEN ENGINE BOOT CONTRACT + PROPOSED BASE FIX

Required format: **specific game → problem → source proof → my proposed fix → coder-only test**. This is not another review of a previously GIF-verified game.

## 1) Target and why this is a real unresolved case
**Game:** Ball2Box, package `com.simondalvai.ball2box`, currently recorded in `docs/VERIFIED_EXECUTED_GAMES.md` as `L0_LOADED_ONLY` in session S83, with no meaningful visual proof. It is not one of the six already GIF-reviewed targets.

Upstream source:
- GitHub mirror: https://github.com/dulvui/ball2box
- Main source moved to Codeberg: https://codeberg.org/dulvui/ball2box
- Source project file: https://github.com/dulvui/ball2box/blob/master/game/project.godot
- Android packaging/source reference: https://github.com/alemart/opensurge-android (similar native-engine Android packaging pattern; do not assume it is the same engine).

I read the actual `game/project.godot` source (blob `5fea37c0864ffaec83c5b768db566fca83249ae1`). It explicitly establishes:
- Godot Engine 3.x project (repository README);
- main scene is `res://src/screens/splah/SplashScreen.tscn`;
- four autoload singletons must initialize before normal scene flow: `BallMachine`, `AudioMachine`, `Global`, `ObjectsUtil`;
- display is portrait 720×1280 with 2D stretch;
- rendering driver is `GLES2`, with fallback to GLES2;
- physics tick rate is 240 FPS.
The repo README also says Godot 3.x and notes a Godot 4 migration had mesh/texture breakage. This is source evidence for a native engine + packaged resource + GLES boot path; it does not itself prove which runtime edge fails in MiniAndroid.

## 2) Specific problem hypothesis
A Godot Android APK is not a normal Android Canvas/View game. Before Ball2Box can show its splash scene, the APK must enter the Godot native engine, locate/load the engine-compatible project data/resources, create a working graphics context, initialize autoload scripts, and render the main scene. A runtime that only gets as far as Activity/process launch can produce L0/blank evidence without having started the game engine meaningfully.

The current MiniAndroid `docs/LOAD_COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX.jsonl` has the native library/JNI layer marked MISSING: `System.loadLibrary` unhandled, no .so extraction, phantom `nativeLibraryDir`, and JNI mostly stubs. It separately records asset opening as BROKEN (fake-success on missing entries, `list()` returning null, no `openFd/openNonAsset`) and graphics support gaps. Those are three distinct possible first divergences; do not collapse them into one “Godot unsupported” label.

## 3) My proposed base-level solution
Reuse the existing UPP-001 native/JNI root, asset root, and graphics roots. Do not add a Ball2Box package-specific branch.

A. **First, prove the exported APK's true requirements.** Inspect its manifest, launcher, APK SHA-256, minSdk, ABI directories, ELF machine, shared-library names, project data / PCK entries, and whether engine and game data are in the same APK or split. If no x86/x86_64 native payload exists, record PREREQUISITE_MISMATCH per project rule; do not call ARM-only a runtime defect.

B. **Make native loading truthful.** Resolve the exact engine library from the installed APK for the active ABI, validate ELF class/machine and dependencies, load it through the shared resolver, and report actual failure. Never treat a stub handler or a “loaded” log as engine initialization.

C. **Make packaged game data truthful.** Asset/PCK/resource lookup must return real bytes or an explicit not-found error. Remove fake-success empty asset streams on this path. Log requested virtual path, APK entry/path, bytes returned, and result. Do not try to unpack/rewrite every asset if the engine expects the original pack format; implement the contract the actual exported APK uses.

D. **Prove graphics separately.** Trace native engine entry → graphics driver/context created → first scene/resource opened → autoload initialization → SplashScreen scene instantiated → first scene draw → app-owned pixels. If engine load succeeds but GLES2 context creation fails, fix the GL/surface path, not JNI. If the context works but the PCK/resource lookup fails, fix the asset/resource contract.

E. **Don't attempt a full Godot interpreter rewrite in this wave.** The minimum meaningful outcome is to identify and reproduce the first missing shared contract and build a small deterministic probe for it. If MiniAndroid has no feasible way to execute Godot's native engine in the current architecture, record that limitation accurately and prioritize generic Android apps/games that can be supported; do not fake a rendered scene.

## 4) Coder-only test plan (not executed by researcher)
1. Locate the exact Ball2Box APK in the local corpus; record APK SHA-256, version, ABI/ELF inventory and current MiniAndroid binary SHA. If absent, record it and choose the smallest already-present Godot/native game instead; don't silently substitute an unrelated APK.

# FOUNDATION 13/4 — SIMPLE CHESS CLOCK (125 KB): SOURCE-BASED FIRST-RENDER CONTRACT + PROPOSED GENERIC FIX

Required format: **specific target → source-confirmed problem/contract → my proposed base fix → coder-only test**. Do not revisit already GIF-reviewed games.

## 1) Exact target and why it is a strong fast probe
**Target:** Simple Chess Clock, package `com.chessclock.android`, version 2.12.0, reported APK size ~125 KB, minSdk 21. Project's verified-execution audit records it as `L0_LOADED_ONLY` / `rendered=false`; audit downgraded it to OBSERVED because a blank frame is not visual evidence.

- Upstream source: https://github.com/simenheg/simple-chess-clock
- Source file: https://github.com/simenheg/simple-chess-clock/blob/master/src/com/chessclock/android/ChessClock.java
- Layout: https://github.com/simenheg/simple-chess-clock/blob/master/res/layout/main.xml
- Manifest: https://github.com/simenheg/simple-chess-clock/blob/master/AndroidManifest.xml
- F-Droid listing corroborates package/version/size/minSdk: https://f-droid.org/packages/com.chessclock.android/

This is a very small, pure-Java, no-engine/no-native candidate. It is ideal for reducing the “blank app” diagnosis to a bounded layout/resource/lifecycle probe before we chase Godot/JNI.

## 2) What source actually proves
At `ChessClock.java:143-154`, `onCreate()` calls:
1. `requestWindowFeature(FEATURE_NO_TITLE)`;
2. `getWindow().addFlags(FLAG_FULLSCREEN)`;
3. `setContentView(R.layout.main)`;
4. `setUpGame(true)`.

The only main UI is `res/layout/main.xml`, a nested `RelativeLayout → LinearLayout(vertical) → two RelativeLayouts` tree. It relies on:
- `layout_weight=1` for the two player areas;
- `layout_width/height=match_parent` and `wrap_content`;
- `layout_above`, `layout_below`, `layout_alignLeft/Right`, and centered children;
- `@color/bg_dark`, `@color/highlight`, other color IDs;
- `@drawable/menu_button` / `pause_button` / `reset_button`;
- two 90sp TextViews with IDs `t_Player1` and `t_Player2`;
- XML `android:onClick="P1ClickHandler"`, `P2ClickHandler`, `MenuListener`, and `PauseListener`.

Then `setUpGame(true)` immediately looks up those views, assigns colors/backgrounds, and writes both clock strings through `setClock(TextView, ...)`. Thus a successful Activity launch is not enough: layout inflation, view IDs, text, color/drawable resource resolution and geometry must all be correct before the app can show a meaningful first frame.

MiniAndroid's current `docs/LOAD_COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX.jsonl` explicitly records:
- `resources_values` BROKEN: missing values can become empty string/black/24px/fake TypedArray instead of a real resolution error;
- `resource_identifier` BROKEN: `getIdentifier` resolves only type `id`, not other resource types.
The existing layout inflater and foundation fixtures mean do not presume all layout is missing. The actual question is whether this *specific APK layout* inflates to the correct tree and bounds, and whether the resources/text survive through the draw pipeline.

## 3) My proposed base-level fix
**First make the existing ViewTree/provenance report decisive for every XML-inflated app.** Before changing code, capture the Chess Clock root tree after `setContentView` and after `setUpGame(true)`, including each view's class, ID, text, visibility, resolved background/text color, layout params, measured bounds, and draw/pixel bounds.

Then apply only the first demonstrated generic defect:
- If IDs or child views are missing: fix APK resource-ID mapping / LayoutInflater instantiation and parent-child attachment, not the game.
- If tree exists but both player panels have zero/overlapping bounds: fix generic `LinearLayout` weight distribution and `RelativeLayout` anchor resolution (measure/layout contract); retain exact Android layout-param semantics.
- If bounds are valid but the screen is still blank: trace `TextView.setText` → Paint/text draw and background color/drawable resolution; fix the first failed resource/draw contract. Do not replace unresolved resources with black/empty defaults.
- If the first frame is correct but taps fail: separately fix XML `android:onClick` binding. Android resolves the named public handler against the context chain at inflation time; preserve the real exception when no handler exists. This is an interaction bug, not a first-render root.
- Keep Handler timing separate: `myHandler.postDelayed(..., TICK_LENGTH)` is used after the initial static UI; do not blame the timer for an initial blank screen unless traces prove the first visible content depends on it.

A useful minimal regression fixture should reproduce the exact structural law: vertical LinearLayout with two weight=1 children; nested RelativeLayouts; above/below and center constraints; 90sp TextViews; color and drawable resources; then assert both player panels and text have nonzero, nonoverlapping bounds and non-background pixels. Reuse the current layout/resource root; no Chess Clock package branch.

## 4) Coder-only test (target ≤120 seconds warm)
1. Find the exact local APK; record APK SHA-256, version, minSdk, ABI/native inventory (expect no native payload but inspect), current MiniAndroid binary SHA, and source revision. If absent, mark absent and use the smallest existing pure-Java layout-heavy L0 target.
2. Run the unchanged APK with a bounded warm probe.
3. Capture checkpoints: Activity.onCreate entry/exit; setContentView inflate result; root/child ViewTree; `findViewById` IDs; `setUpGame(true)`; both `setClock` results; resolved colors/drawables; measure/layout rectangles; TextView draw calls; screenshot SHA and app-owned pixel count.
4. Negative control: remove one referenced drawable/resource in a synthetic fixture and require explicit resource-not-found, not silent black/empty fallback.
5. Positive control: a tiny equivalent layout must show two large time strings and two distinguishable panels with stable pixel hashes across 3 runs.
6. If layout/resource root is reproduced, fix the shared code and replay Chess Clock plus one independent XML-heavy Java app. If it is not reproduced, report FALSIFIED and move to the actual first divergence (lifecycle, text draw, etc.). Do not run the full battery just to identify the first edge; run the fast fixture first, then required regressions after the patch.

## 5) Exact result contract
Return:
`APK SHA | source revision | first failed checkpoint | tree/bounds/resource evidence | existing root reused | proposed local diff | negative/positive fixture | pre/post pixel evidence | second-app fan-out | status`.

Valid outcomes: `LAYOUT_ROOT_REPRODUCED`, `RESOURCE_ROOT_REPRODUCED`, `TEXT_DRAW_ROOT_REPRODUCED`, `INTERACTION_ONLY`, `FALSIFIED`, `PREREQUISITE_MISMATCH`, or `BLOCKED` with evidence. Keep this in #364; no new issue. The source proves what must be displayed; it does not yet prove which runtime defect caused the recorded blank frame. Coder must execute the APK test before any root is called confirmed.

# FOUNDATION 14/4 — FIVE-APK BATCH, NOT ONE-APP-AT-A-TIME: FIRST-DIVERGENCE TRIAGE + SOURCE-GROUNDED FIXES

Owner correction: every wave must cover **at least five actual APKs in one batch**. Do not spend a turn on one game, and do not run a full multi-minute battery per candidate just to locate the first failure. Reuse the 1–2 minute probe requested in FOUNDATION 6/4. This batch is five independent app/game paths, chosen from current non-rendered or incomplete corpus evidence; they are not the six previously GIF-reviewed games.

## 1) The five targets and my source-based diagnosis

### A. Memory — `eu.quelltext.memory` — WebView/local HTML
Source: https://github.com/niccokunzmann/app.memory.quelltext.eu and https://github.com/niccokunzmann/memory.quelltext.eu
Source facts: FullscreenActivity loads `file:///android_asset/memory.quelltext.eu/index.html`; the WebView is the app's main content. The HTML has many dependent classic scripts marked `async`. The current runtime matrix records WebView load callbacks missing and localStorage as memory-only.
**Candidate first failure:** HTML/script/asset load or async dependency race.
**My proposed fix:** trace each URL/resource request and JS exception; if the app-source race is confirmed, A/B a source build using ordered `defer` scripts. For runtime, implement truthful document/load/error callbacks and correct relative local-asset resolution; do not force async execution order globally.
Test evidence required: DOM/load state, script exceptions, asset bytes, first non-background pixels.

### B. Simple Chess Clock — `com.chessclock.android` — XML View tree
Source: https://github.com/simenheg/simple-chess-clock
Source facts: `onCreate()` calls `setContentView(R.layout.main)` and `setUpGame(true)`. The layout uses nested LinearLayout/RelativeLayout, weight=1, anchor constraints, TextViews, color/drawable resources and XML `android:onClick`. Runtime matrix records fake defaults for unresolved values and incomplete dynamic resource identifiers.
**Candidate first failure:** incorrect inflation/measure/layout/resource resolution, not native engine.
**My proposed fix:** emit ViewTree provenance with IDs, text, resources and measured bounds; patch only the first demonstrated shared contract. Do not silently replace missing resources with black/empty defaults.
Test evidence: both clock panels/text have nonzero, non-overlapping bounds and visible pixels; interactions are a separate check.

### C. Ball2Box — `com.simondalvai.ball2box` — Godot 3 / GLES2
Source: https://github.com/dulvui/ball2box and https://codeberg.org/dulvui/ball2box
Source facts from `game/project.godot`: main scene `SplashScreen.tscn`, four autoload singletons, portrait 720×1280, GLES2. Runtime matrix says native/JNI, packaged assets and graphics each have gaps.
**Candidate first failure:** engine .so/ABI, project resource/PCK read, or GLES context. These are separate checkpoints.
**My proposed fix:** inspect APK ELF/ABI before testing; for supported x86/x86_64 payload, require real library resolution, actual asset bytes/errors and a separate GL-context trace. If ARM-only, mark prerequisite mismatch, not a runtime bug.
Test evidence: engine entry, PCK/resource open, context creation, scene initialization, first app-owned pixels.

### D. Open Surge — `org.opensurge2d.surgeengine` — native 2D engine / Allegro
Android wrapper: https://github.com/alemart/opensurge-android
Engine source: https://github.com/alemart/opensurge
Source facts: `MainActivity.java` loads a chain of native libraries (`physfs`, `allegro`, primitives, image, font, TTF, audio, codec and others) via `System.loadLibrary`, and passes `libopensurge.so` to its Allegro activity. Engine source separates subsystem initialization, asset/resource managers, initial scene and video/GLES initialization. Android build explicitly requires GLES support.
**Candidate first failure:** native dependency chain, native engine entry, asset virtual filesystem, or GLES. A single “activity launched” result cannot tell which.
**My proposed fix:** add ordered loader-state/dependency trace and engine checkpoints; no fake-success on any missing .so/resource. Stop at the first failing library or engine stage. This shares UPP-001 and asset/graphics roots; no app-specific branch.
Test evidence: each required library's ELF/ABI and load result, engine init, asset lookup, GLES context, initial scene and first game pixels.

### E. Guandan — `page.codeberg.lanticy.guandan` — card game / app framework
Source listing: https://codeberg.org/lanticy/guandan ; F-Droid: https://f-droid.org/packages/page.codeberg.lanticy.guandan/
Current project registry records this title as `L2_GRAPHICALLY_INCOMPLETE` in S83. Its public description identifies a four-player card game over local Wi-Fi. I could verify the project identity and current evidence row, but could not fetch its Codeberg source through the GitHub connector; therefore do not invent implementation details.
**Candidate first failure:** still unknown until APK manifest/DEX and runtime first-divergence trace identify its UI toolkit, entry Activity, resource and drawing path.
**My proposed fix:** no app-specific code change yet. First classify the APK and use ViewTree/provenance or native-engine checkpoints selected from actual source/DEX evidence. Then tie the first failed framework contract to a shared root. If it requires network peers before displaying a board, test offline/local startup separately from rendering.
Test evidence: first Activity content, first visible card/board region, any network wait/error, and whether the game can render a local empty/new-game board without a peer.

## 2) One shared fast probe for all five
Run all five through the same warm probe (target ≤120 seconds per batch/candidate; no full battery before root discovery). Emit one machine-readable row per APK:
`package | apk_sha256 | version | ABI/ELF | launcher/toolkit | first failed checkpoint | exact exception/trace | source contract | existing root | status | next action`.

The probe must collect, where applicable:
1. Activity entry/exit and first exception;
2. layout/ViewTree or WebView/native-engine entry;
3. requested resources/assets and real byte count / explicit failure;
4. surface/context or draw-call progress;
5. app-owned non-background pixel count and screenshot SHA.

Do not force every app through every stage: use capability-aware checkpoints and stop at its first relevant failure. For native apps, ABI preflight is mandatory; ARM-only candidates are PREREQUISITE_MISMATCH and do not count as runtime failures. For source-unavailable Guandan, explicitly mark source inspection pending and ground the diagnosis in APK/DEX/trace.

## 3) Root-fix decision across the batch
- If two or more apps stop at the same exact semantic violation, implement one generic root fix and replay all five.
- If failures differ, record separate first-divergence rows and do not bundle unrelated fixes.
- Keep app-source bugs (e.g. Memory async dependency ordering) separate from runtime bugs.
- Use tiny deterministic fixtures for each discovered law so future triage becomes a 1–2 minute test rather than hours/days.
- After a fix, require positive + negative fixture and a second-app fan-out check; only then run the established regression battery.

## 4) Acceptance gate
The coder must comment back with five APK rows and traces, plus source links, ABI disposition, exact root reused, proposed/local diff, before/after screenshot/pixel evidence and regression result. If any target APK is absent, substitute another non-GIF-reviewed corpus APK and record why. Do not return a prose-only “tested” claim; no new issue, continue in #364.

# FOUNDATION 15/4 — FIVE REAL CORPUS GAMES: CUSTOM-VIEW / DRAWABLE / IMAGE-DECODE / KORGE FIRST-PAINT AUDIT

This wave corrects the scaling problem: **five existing corpus packages in one batch**, source inspection first, one common fast probe, and no full regression run until a first semantic failure is found. These are not the six GIF-reviewed titles. Current `docs/VERIFIED_EXECUTED_GAMES.md` records all five as OBSERVED near-blank/incomplete candidates in S85/S87; that is evidence to investigate, not proof of a particular bug.

## Target batch and source-backed contracts

### 1. Sudoku — `org.secuso.privacyfriendlysudoku`
Corpus row: L1 `NONBLANK_NEARBLANK_GATE`, S85.
Source: https://github.com/SecUSo/privacy-friendly-sudoku
Files:
- `ui/view/SudokuFieldLayout.java`: creates a 2D array of `SudokuCellView`, attaches each as a child, obtains style attributes through `obtainStyledAttributes`, and calls `setWillNotDraw(false)`.
- `ui/view/SudokuCellView.java`: custom `onDraw(Canvas)`, creates `Paint`, draws cell backgrounds and values; reads many custom styleable colors.
**Candidate problem:** custom View canvas path or custom `TypedArray` styleable resolution can leave the grid blank/near-blank even when Activity launches.
**My proposed fix:** do not add a Sudoku-specific path. Add a generic custom-View first-paint probe recording measured bounds, `willNotDraw`, `onDraw` entry/exit, canvas operation count, resolved styleable indices/colors, and pixels emitted. If attributes fall back incorrectly, fix generic `obtainStyledAttributes/TypedArray`; if onDraw never runs or draws no pixels, fix invalidation/draw traversal. Do not presume which branch is broken.

### 2. Privacy Friendly Memo Game — `org.secuso.privacyfriendlymemory`
Corpus row: L1 `NONBLANK_NEARBLANK_GATE`, S85.
Source: https://github.com/SecUSo/privacy-friendly-memo-game
File `ui/MemoImageAdapter.java`: creates/reuses `ImageView` cells for a `GridView`, uses `BitmapFactory`, resolves custom image URIs, caches decoded bitmaps, and has a fallback `notFoundBitmap` decoded from an `android.resource://...` URI.
**Candidate problem:** URI-to-resource resolution / BitmapFactory decode / GridView adapter binding may silently turn real card images into null/empty/fallback images.
**My proposed fix:** instrument the shared URI resolver and bitmap decoder with URI, resource owner package, stream byte count, decode result/dimensions, and chosen adapter position. Missing URI/resource must be explicit, not a fake empty bitmap. Fix only the first demonstrated generic URI/resource/decode contract; preserve the app's fallback behavior when the app itself chooses it.

### 3. Privacy Friendly Dame — `org.secuso.privacyfriendlydame`
Corpus row: L1 `NONBLANK_NEARBLANK_GATE`, S85.
Source: https://github.com/SecUSo/privacy-friendly-dame
Files `ui/CheckersLayout.java` and `ui/GameActivity.kt`: Activity calls `setContentView(R.layout.activity_game)`, constructs `CheckersLayout(game, this)`, calls `refresh()`, and inserts the board into main/side content layouts. `CheckersLayout` builds board cells as `AppCompatImageView` instances and uses resource-backed colors/backgrounds.
**Candidate problem:** programmatically created children may be constructed and refreshed but have bad bounds, absent drawable layers, or unresolved resource colors.
**My proposed fix:** ViewTree provenance should include dynamically attached children, drawable class/layers/alpha/filter, bounds and pixel contribution after `refresh()`. Fix generic child layout / drawable / color resolution if trace proves the break. Do not synthesize checker pieces from package name.

### 4. Privacy Friendly Solitaire — `org.secuso.privacyfriendlysolitaire`
Corpus row: L1 `NONBLANK_NEARBLANK_GATE`, S85.
Source: https://github.com/SecUSo/privacy-friendly-solitaire
Its Android manifest declares a launcher `.Activities.SplashActivity`, followed by `.Activities.MainActivity`, and requires an accelerometer feature. This means launch and the actual game surface are separate stages; do not mark the splash as game-render success. The repository layout has an older Android structure, so the coder must match the local APK version to the source revision before applying source-level conclusions.
**Candidate problem:** splash-to-main Activity transition, orientation/configuration handling, or required sensor/launch precondition could prevent reaching the actual game board.
**My proposed fix:** trace launcher Activity lifecycle and explicit/implicit transition to MainActivity; record exact exception or missing capability. Verify local manifest/version and whether the game screen is actually reached before inspecting board draw. If the installed APK's required accelerometer is unavailable in the harness, classify the exact prerequisite rather than inventing a rendering fix.

### 5. 2048 — `org.andstatus.game2048`
Corpus row: L1 `NONBLANK_NEARBLANK_GATE`, S85.
Source: https://github.com/andstatus/game2048
Source `src/commonMain/kotlin/org/andstatus/game2048/Main.kt` calls KorGE `Korge(...){ myLog("Stage is ready"); viewData(this) }`; it computes a virtual size from the window aspect ratio. `view/BoardView.kt` builds board graphics with KorGE `roundRect`, `graphics`, `solidRect`, and swipe/updater handlers.
**Candidate problem:** Android Activity/process launch may succeed while KorGE Stage setup, virtual-size calculation, graphics commands or frame presentation never reaches the host surface.
**My proposed fix:** add generic KorGE/native-renderer lifecycle checkpoints: engine entry, Stage ready, virtual/window size, scene child count, draw command count, frame submitted, and host surface/pixel receipt. If Stage is ready but host gets no pixels, fix renderer/surface presentation; if stage never becomes ready, fix engine bootstrap. Do not treat the `Stage is ready` log alone as rendered proof.

## Shared 1–2 minute probe, all five in one wave
Run a single harness command/config over these five local APKs. Before execution, record local APK SHA-256, version, source revision confidence, minSdk, ABI/native inventory and current binary SHA. If any APK is missing, report it and substitute another non-GIF-reviewed corpus APK in the same family; do not silently count a missing app as tested.

Emit one JSONL row per app with:
`package, apk_sha256, binary_sha, source_match, first_activity, first_failed_edge, exact_exception, viewtree_or_stage_state, resource_uri_and_bytes, drawable_or_canvas_ops, measured_bounds, app_owned_pixel_count, screenshot_sha, status`.

The probe should be capability-aware and stop at the first failed edge. For View-based games, record layout/custom View/drawable/bitmap state. For KorGE, record stage/virtual size/draw/frame submission. Do not force a single Android View probe onto KorGE.

## Decision rule and proposed base fix
- If Sudoku and Dame both fail at generic custom-view/draw traversal, create one minimal custom-View fixture and fix that root.
- If Memo and another target fail at URI/resource/bitmap resolution, create one local-resource URI + bitmap decode fixture and fix that root.
- If only Solitaire fails before MainActivity, investigate lifecycle/manifest/sensor prerequisite, not rendering.
- If only 2048 fails after Stage ready, isolate frame/surface presentation from View drawing.
- If failures differ, record five separate first-divergence rows and do not bundle them.
- Each fix must have a tiny positive fixture and a negative control; rerun the five-app batch before the expensive regression suite. Target diagnosis latency: ≤120 seconds per app on a warm run.

## Coder-only result requirement
Comment back in this same issue with all five rows, exact local APK SHA/version, trace excerpts, confirmed/falsified root, minimal test fixture, proposed/local diff, pre/post pixel evidence and whether a second independent app passes. Source review is done for the contracts above; **the APK tests have not been run by me**, so none of these hypotheses is labeled confirmed. No new issue and no app-specific compatibility hacks.

## 2. F-NEW-376 — staged-generation install atomicity law (ROOT-CAUSED-FIXED, P1)

**The law (one canonical commit point):** the COMPLETE new generation — `base.apk` + `package.json` + `lib/<abi>/` + `native_libs.json` — is built under `<store>/data/app/.staging/<pkg>.<pid>`; the staged bytes are sha-verified against the source; then the generation commits by a directory switch:
- **fresh install:** ONE `rename(staging → live)` — the whole commit is atomic.
- **update:** park old → `.trash/<pkg>.<pid>`, promote new, drop parked. POSIX `rename()` cannot atomically replace a non-empty directory (ENOTEMPTY), so the two-rename window is unavoidable — and is **closed by rollback**: any promotion failure renames the parked old generation back to live; if rollback itself fails, the wave hard-errors and reports the preserved trash path. Both window behaviors are fault-injection-proven below.
- The staged record is **byte-identical after promotion** (shared `record_json_body` writer describes the LIVE location; no post-promotion rewrite). Readers (`run --package`, `list-packages`, `pkgaudit`, `pkginspect`) resolve only committed generations; `.staging`/`.trash` are hidden from listing. Data-dir scaffolding moved post-commit.

**Deterministic fault-injection capability (env-gated, generic):** `MINIANDROID_INSTALL_FAULT=stage_copy|stage_hash|record_write|lib_extract|promote|promote_mid|cleanup`. `stage_hash` injects a REAL byte flip into the staged copy (the integrity gate must catch it — positive control, not a simulated skip).

- **`Lzs.m`** = the kotlin-stdlib continuation machine (literal *"call to 'resume' before 'invoke' with coroutine"*, `COROUTINE_SUSPENDED` sentinel `Lwr;->e`, direct unintercepted delegate call).
- **The unwind is FAITHFUL ART behavior**: it passed through the measure frames and was **terminally contained by the machinery's own typed catch (`Llo.B`)** — the exception never escaped the engine. `[EXC-UNWIND]` rows `run/cont75/dooz_cfd` unchanged.

**Verdict: ✅ root CONFIRMED (decode-complete) · ❌ the named "continuation-boundary conversion" engine law is REJECTED with reason** — the dex machinery already contains the abort; a boundary conversion would *swallow legal control flow* (violates the loop's no-swallow red line), and the engine is not the diverging layer. The real divergence is upstream state: *why* a flow abort fires while the collect is nested inside the measure pass — which is **F-NEW-277's runner-re-arm domain**. The lever order recorded in CONT-75 ("cancellation conversion FIRST") is hereby **corrected to: F-NEW-277 re-arm first**.

### 1.2 F-NEW-379 (P2) — kotlin-reflect CNFE: REJECTED as content blocker (fresh current-HEAD A/B ×3 apps)

The CNFE is kotlin-stdlib's **intentional fallback path** (try `ReflectionFactoryImpl`, catch CNFE, fall back to the base factory). **All three apps catch it and proceed.** Verdict: **❌ REJECTED_WITH_REASON — no shim needed.** The REAL blockers, named for the next wave: Guandan = empty composition (`AndroidComposeView children=0`, dark surface 1 color `8,36,26` — the F-NEW-277/378 family); AndStatus2048 = NPE `Object.getClass` on null in `Lt60;.getValue` / `Ll90;.u` pc=160 (kotlin-delegate chain — new candidate, decode pending).

## 3. F-NEW-380 (NEW, ROOT-CAUSED-FIXED P0): beginRecording accumulate-amplification

**AOSP law:** `RecordingCanvas.beginRecording` — *"the previous recording is discarded"* — every record starts a **fresh display list**. The engine appended to the node's prior op list instead.

Runtime proof chain:
1. `[C77-RECORD] node=9348 prior_ops=1..9 growing within one frame` (re-record accumulation, direct evidence).
2. `MINIANDROID_CANVAS_OP_TRACE` pre-fix stream: **2471 ops with 1562 identical `New game` TEXT ops** at (765,1829.976) + 189 `Dooz` ops — **all from the single paint site `Lj7;.e`** (compose MultiParagraph; chain `Lj7.e ← Lj7.f ← Lwu0.i ← Lnt1.Q ← Lgl0.c`, stack depth 157–164; caller attribution via the extended S81 diag).
3. Mechanism: accumulate at beginRecording → `drawRenderNode` replay copies ever-growing lists per level → the compose draw burns the whole wall budget re-recording duplicate content → frame never completes → F-NEW-298 keeps the splash.
4. **Fix (generic):** `render_nodes_[recv].clear()` at `beginRecording`. Post-fix stream: **2477 ops, ZERO flood rows**. No app/R8-specific logic; re-recording is idempotent under any invalidation cadence.

# CONT-78 DIRECTIVE — Expand real APK/game execution coverage (not another research-only wave)

The user's priority is explicit: **make more real programs and games actually run and show app-owned content**. Continue inside this same master Issue #364; do not create a disconnected issue or declare completion.

## 0. Before touching code: synchronize and establish truth
- Fetch and fast-forward to `origin/main`; record full HEAD, clean/dirty state, deterministic build command, runtime binary SHA-256, registry count, and current corpus manifest hash.
- Read the latest #364 comments and current source/registry for F-NEW-381, F-NEW-277, and the four wrapper-unwrapping residuals. Revalidate these against current HEAD; do not inherit stale conclusions blindly.
- Preserve all existing gates. Never use a blank/splash/background-only screenshot, APK parse success, or clean exit as evidence that an app works.

## 1. The deliverable is a larger executed corpus
Use the existing `scripts/cont76_semantic_probe.py` / shared semantic-probe infrastructure (or improve it generically if needed) to execute **at least 25 additional distinct APKs in this wave**, targeting **30+ total distinct apps/games across the current and new evidence set**. Aim for at least 15 games and 10 non-game apps, with x86/x86_64 APKs prioritized. ARM-only/native-ABI mismatches must be marked `PREREQUISITE_MISMATCH`, not counted as runtime rendering failures and not silently substituted.

Choose candidates from the repository's existing corpus/registry and available APKs, not made-up names. Prefer a broad, stratified sample:
- simple native/View-based games and board/puzzle games;
- games with Canvas/Bitmap/Path/custom View drawing;
- apps exercising resources, assets, files, preferences, SQLite, URI/provider, lifecycle/fragments;
- Kotlin/Compose apps, including but not limited to the known blank family;

Do not merely install 25 APKs. Never merge these into one generic “pass” number.

For at least 5 representative interactive targets, drive real input through the runtime and verify state/content change (board move, button, navigation, timer, preference, etc.). A launch-only face is not interactive proof. Re-run each claimed success 3 times where the existing test contract requires reproducibility.

## 2. Root-cause and fix loop — batch by shared law
Group failures by their **first divergence**, not by APK name. Require at least 5 distinct candidates per diagnosis pass, then choose the highest-fan-out root that is demonstrably reachable in current-head traces. Prefer a generic framework/runtime law fix over app-specific compatibility shims.

Priority order:
1. Measure and fix F-NEW-381 only if a small reproducible benchmark proves the register-file change materially reduces dooz's time-to-content without breaking semantics; otherwise keep it classified and move to another proven high-fan-out root.
2. Re-open F-NEW-277 from current source and traces: determine why the Compose runner/measure path reaches quiescence or triggers AbortFlow control flow; establish a minimal fixture before changing semantics.
3. Test the four recorded wrapper-unwrapping residuals (`RecordingCanvas.drawBitmap` bitmap unresolved ×2, `Path.addRoundRect` RectF unresolved, `clipPath` path unresolved) against actual consumers and minimal positive/negative fixtures. Fix shared unwrapping only if the fixtures identify a generic boundary-law gap.
4. Search the expanded corpus for a repeated root appearing in at least two unrelated APKs. A single-app symptom is not enough for a broad shim unless its framework contract itself proves the defect.

## 3. Mandatory evidence and anti-fake-success gates
- Preserve and run the existing regression battery: wall A/B zero drift, goldens, negative tests, reinstall, c72priv/privacy, MG-310, MG-150, and s82 validator.
- Record before/after binary SHA and screenshot/pixel evidence for every runtime change.

- If a target cannot be executed because its APK is missing or ABI-incompatible, state that precisely and continue to the next valid corpus candidate; do not let prerequisites consume the whole wave.
- Keep the working tree clean, commit source + tests + evidence + registry/docs together, push to `origin/main`, and verify remote HEAD after push.

## 4. Required CONT-78 report in this issue
1. Start/end HEAD, binary SHA, build reproducibility, tree state.
2. Exact list of at least 25 new APKs actually executed, with the evidence columns above.
3. Total unique apps/games tested to date and counts/percentages for each verdict category; explicitly distinguish launch content from interactive verification.

6. Remaining blockers with evidence, not optimistic labels.
7. Explicit statement of what did **not** run or could not be proven.

**Stop condition:** do not report “complete” merely because 25 launches were attempted. # CONT-78 AUDIT ADDENDUM — fix the measurement harness before trusting the expanded coverage percentage

I inspected the current default-branch source of `scripts/cont76_semantic_probe.py` (blob `4984a8d01eb1b7b37ba8b5abad7e529d4b75df95`). The harness is a useful starting point, but **it cannot yet substantiate all of CONT-78's required claims**. Treat this as a concrete source audit, not a claim that the wave has run.

## Source-grounded gaps to address in CONT-78

1. **Verdict vocabulary is incomplete.** The runner currently emits `REAL_APP_UI`, `SPLASH_ONLY`, `WHITE_BLANK`, `DARK_SURFACE_NO_OPS`, `PREREQUISITE_MISMATCH`, `NO_SCREEN`, and `PARTIAL_MARGINAL`. It does not distinguish `DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_ONLY` from other dark surfaces, does not report `INTERACTIVE_CONTENT_VERIFIED`, and has no explicit `HARNESS/ENVIRONMENT_FAILURE`. Add a versioned normalized mapping; preserve raw legacy verdicts so historical evidence is not silently rewritten.

2. **Pixel richness is not proof of app-owned content.** `classify()` labels a screenshot `REAL_APP_UI` from pixel thresholds alone (`nonbg_ratio >= 0.02` and `unique_colors >= 64`). Keep those metrics as useful signals, but require correlated runtime evidence (window/root ownership, app draw ops or ViewTree/content provenance) before claiming app-owned UI. A splash, debug overlay, or host artifact must not count as a successful app.

3. **Install/run failures can be misclassified.** The code records `install_rc` but proceeds to `run` regardless; a failed install or missing output becomes `NO_SCREEN`, not a harness/install failure. Separate install failure, APK/toolchain failure, runtime crash, budget timeout, and valid app-level blank/splash outcomes. Preserve stdout/stderr, exit status, termination reason, and exact command for every row.

4. **Evidence is too thin for the required diagnosis.** Each row currently stores package, APK SHA-16, binary SHA-16, screenshot SHA-16 and a small pixel census. Extend it with versionCode/versionName, ABI/native-library inventory, install/run command and rc, full screenshot SHA-256, first-missing-stage / first-divergence, relevant trace excerpts, content provenance, state-change proof, root ID, and next action. Store per-app logs/evidence instead of only a summary row.

5. **The current runner does not test interaction or reproducibility.** It does one bounded warm run per APK and accepts no input plan. Add an explicit interaction manifest/driver for at least five representative apps, with before/after state or image comparison and actual dispatched-input evidence. Repeat claimed stable results three times where required. Do not infer interactivity from a colourful launch screenshot.

6. **Audit the hard-coded runtime paths.** `ROOT = "/home/z/my-project"` makes the tool environment-specific. Resolve the repository root from the script location or require a validated CLI/env override; fail early with an explicit harness error if the binary/toolchain is absent. This prevents a wrong-root run from contaminating corpus results.

7. **The denominator must be honest.** Report distinct APK SHA and distinct package counts separately. Do not count retries as new apps; do not count ARM-only prerequisites as renderer failures; do not count harness failures in the app-success numerator. Show both raw totals and category percentages, including the number excluded for prerequisites or harness failures.

## Acceptance gate
Before the 25-APK batch, add focused harness self-tests covering: install failure, no screenshot, splash, white blank, app-owned dark background with no draw ops, rich pixels without app provenance, genuine content with provenance, ABI refusal, timeout/budget exhaustion, and interactive before/after change. Then run the expanded corpus. The harness change itself must pass the existing regression gates and must not alter runtime behavior.

This is an enabling fix, not a reason to stop at tooling. After the measurement contract is trustworthy, CONT-78 must still execute the requested additional APKs and show whether the count of `REAL_APP_CONTENT` and `INTERACTIVE_CONTENT_VERIFIED` actually increases.

# CONT-79 — White/blank-screen ROOT FIX batch (minimum 5 independent roots, one coordinated wave)

**User directive:** fully re-read the historical no-launch/white-screen evidence and resolve at least five high-impact problems in this same #364 wave. Do not create another issue. Search source and public references across languages (English, Chinese, Russian, etc.), but external projects are references—not proof that MiniAndroid has the same defect. The deliverable is code-level root fixes and more real apps/games displaying their own content, not another research-only report.

## First: re-read the actual project evidence, not just the latest summary
Read in full and reconcile against current HEAD:
- `docs/WHITE_SCREEN_LOADING_ROOTS.md`
- `docs/WORKING_APP_LOADING_EXPLANATIONS.md`
- `docs/WORKING_VS_FAILING_LOADING_MATRIX.jsonl`

Record current HEAD and whether every old conclusion is still reproducible. Do not mark all white screens as loading bugs: the historical matrix explicitly says sudoku/WhatsApp were `WINDOW_ROOT`/window-content-chain failures, Telegram settings was `ACTIVITY_NAVIGATION`, opencalc's old empty shell was `VIEW_BIND` (later closed), and dooz was Compose. Preserve that first-missing-stage distinction.

## Required batch: investigate and close at least five problem tracks

### P0-A — F-NEW-277: Compose frame/re-arm/measure path (cross-app blank screens)
Current evidence says dooz's frame pump re-arms, recomposition #2 re-enters NavHost, and AndroidComposeView replays 926 operations after F-NEW-380, yet a frame still fails to complete inside 30s; Guandan has an empty composition root, and the F-NEW-378 AbortFlowException is legal Kotlin flow control that was already caught by the app's typed handler. Do NOT swallow/convert AbortFlowException.
- Build the smallest source/DEX fixture that distinguishes: frame scheduling, composition invalidation, measure/layout, draw recording, budget halt, and presentation.
- Run the same stage probes on dooz + Guandan + at least one unrelated Compose app from the existing corpus.
- Fix the first shared MiniAndroid divergence only if at least two unrelated apps reproduce it. Add positive/negative fixtures and prove the actual first completed content frame—not merely more operations or a changed splash hash.

### P0-B — F-NEW-381: interpreter throughput blocks first content frame
CONT-77 reports dooz needs about 10–12M interpreted instructions at ~310K instructions/sec and hits the 30s budget; the current hypothesis is the large `DalvikValue` representation with two `std::string` fields copied through register operations. This is a high-impact performance blocker, but the proposed representation change is NOT yet a proven fix.
- Profile representative real app launch paths and benchmark the existing representation against a tagged-union/out-of-band-string prototype (or another measured design).
- Preserve Java/Dalvik value semantics, object/string lifetime, exceptions, arrays, reflection, and wide values. Add differential semantic tests before choosing a design.
- Acceptance: show repeated time-to-first-app-content and instruction throughput for dooz and at least two other instruction-heavy apps; require a material improvement, no semantic drift, and the entire anchor battery. If the hypothesis does not win, revert the prototype and publish the measured alternative.

### P0-C — F-NEW-233 / WINDOW_ROOT: sudoku and WhatsApp no root/window-content chain
The historical white-screen audit explicitly says these faces were NOT caused by file loading. Find the earliest missing edge in Activity → Window/DecorView → WindowManager/ViewRoot → content parent → measure/layout/draw. Check lifecycle ordering, content attachment, visibility, measured dimensions, and traversal scheduling at the source level.
- Compare sudoku + WhatsApp traces with a known-good View-based app at the same checkpoints.
- Fix the common framework/lifecycle law if shared; do not special-case package names and do not count a root object merely existing as success.
- Acceptance: both targets reach an attached, visible, non-zero content tree and produce app-owned drawing operations plus non-background screenshot content on three clean runs; if not, state the exact earliest divergence and why the two cases differ.

### P1-D — Canvas/Path wrapper-boundary residuals (multiple custom-drawing apps/games)
The latest open notes name `RecordingCanvas.drawBitmap` bitmap unresolved (two call sites), `Path.addRoundRect` RectF unresolved, and `clipPath` path unresolved. These can affect many games and custom Views.
- Find all call sites and the interpreter-to-native/framework argument conversion path. Do not patch each method independently if the generic wrapper-unwrapping law is wrong.
- Create minimal positive and negative fixtures for object wrapper → underlying bitmap/path/RectF identity, nulls, overload selection, and lifetime; then validate against at least five corpus candidates that exercise custom Canvas/Path/Bitmap drawing.
- Acceptance: the fixture proves correct pixels/clipping, and at least two unrelated APKs improve without regressions. If a named residual is unreachable or already fixed at current HEAD, prove that and replace it with the next repeated drawing failure.

### P1-E — AndStatus2048 delegate-chain NPE / empty-state screen
CONT-76 records a real post-CNFE failure: `Object.getClass` on null in `Lt60;.getValue` / `Ll90;.u` pc=160. The CNFE itself is a valid Kotlin reflection fallback and must not receive a shim.
- Decode the caller/callee and determine whether the null is legal uninitialized delegate state, missing initialization order, a missing framework return value, or an interpreter semantic defect.
- Add a minimal fixture for the proven law, then compare AndStatus2048 with Guandan and at least one unrelated Kotlin/delegate app. Fix only the common semantic defect; do not invent a non-null default.

### P1-F — App content is visible but interaction/state transition fails (game/app usability)
Expand beyond launch faces: use the existing MG-150 transform/hit-test fence and real corpus. Verify event dispatch, transformed coordinates, View hit-testing, click/listener delivery, and state-to-next-frame invalidation as one end-to-end chain. Select at least five existing apps/games, send real taps/gestures, and prove board/UI/state change. A green isolated hit-test fixture is not proof that real app interaction works.

## External source reading (cross-language research; use to check contracts, not copy implementation blindly)
- AOSP RenderNode source (English, authoritative): https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/master/graphics/java/android/graphics/RenderNode.java
- Android official Compose phases and first-frame/recomposition failure patterns: https://developer.android.com/agents/skills/jetpack-compose/jetpack-compose-performance/references/state-and-stability
- Chinese Activity/Window/ViewRootImpl/Surface lifecycle walkthrough (cross-check the lifecycle chain against AOSP source): https://github.com/ChenSiLiang/android-toy/blob/master/%E5%89%96%E6%9E%90Activity%E3%80%81Window%E3%80%81ViewRootImpl%E5%92%8CView%E4%B9%8B%E9%97%B4%E7%9A%84%E5%85%B3%E7%B3%BB/%E5%89%96%E6%9E%90Activity%E3%80%81Window%E3%80%81ViewRootImpl%E5%92%8CView%E4%B9%8B%E9%97%B4%E7%9A%84%E5%85%B3%E7%B3%BB.md
- AOSP ART interpreter cache/performance source: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/art/+/d7c74b43f850c4f725f406023a57f0d978607c5a/runtime/interpreter/interpreter_cache.h
- Public blank-screen reports are only comparison cases, not evidence about MiniAndroid: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/149328 and https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/160647

Search additional Chinese/Russian/English GitHub issues and source for each track. For every external finding, record the upstream version/contract, whether MiniAndroid implements the same contract, and a local reproducer. Do not claim a source search proves a root cause by itself.

## Execution breadth and priority
- Execute at least 5 distinct APKs per diagnosis cluster; use at least 10 additional valid x86/x86_64 APKs in this wave if the corpus/artifacts permit. Do not count missing APKs or ARM-only prerequisite mismatches as runtime failures.
- Choose the highest-fan-out confirmed root first, but deliver a verdict for all six tracks in this single coordinated request. “Investigated” is not “fixed”; statuses must remain ROOT_CAUSED_FIXED / CONFIRMED_NOT_FIXED / REJECTED_WITH_EVIDENCE / BLOCKED with proof.
- Keep a before/after binary SHA, screenshot SHA-256 + pixel metrics, first-missing-stage trace, app-owned draw/content provenance, and three-run repeatability for every claimed win.
- Preserve the current regressions: wall A/B zero drift, goldens, negatives, reinstall, c72priv/privacy, MG-310, MG-150, and s82 validator. Add the new fixtures to the same regression entrypoint.
- Do not update goldens just to make tests green. No package-name branches, blank-screen fake closure, “more draw ops” as a success metric, or claims based solely on install/exit code.
- Push code, fixtures, test runner, evidence and registry/doc updates to origin/main. Then post one concise scoreboard in #364 showing each of the six tracks, apps actually fixed, apps still blank, interactive wins, regressions, and what was not proven.

**Definition of done for this wave:** at least five root tracks have evidence-backed terminal verdicts; multiple unrelated real apps improve in the same wave; the total count of apps with verified app-owned content and verified interaction increases; all existing gates remain green. Do not call the whole #364 issue complete while major blockers remain.

# CONT-80 — Five NEW high-fan-out execution/blank-screen roots (separate from CONT-79)

This is a continuation inside #364, not a new issue. These five tracks are intentionally **additional** to the six tracks in CONT-79 (Compose, DEX throughput, WindowRoot for Sudoku/WhatsApp, Canvas/Path wrappers, AndStatus2048 delegate NPE, and interaction). Re-read and validate the evidence against current HEAD before modifying anything; historical documents have divergent baselines and must not be treated as current-head proof.

## Evidence basis already present in this repository
- docs/DIFFERENTIAL_WORKING_VS_WHITE.md describes five distinct white-screen families: Fossify Clock (EventBus/onCreate + null XmlPullParser/inflater, no authoritative WindowRoot), BlockBlast (ComposeView missing from class index), Asteroids Revenge (Arrays.toString shadow returns null before GodotView creation), SpaceVertex (Kotlin reflection fallback + Fragment instantiation contract), SanskritBasics Memory (null framework receiver during AndroidX WindowInsets/ActionBarOverlayLayout initialization).
- docs/knowledge/graphics/GRAPHICS_ROOT_CAUSES.md records F-NEW-159 null framework receivers and F-NEW-157 GLSurfaceView/EGL/swapBuffers absent, with 35-title and libGDX families respectively.
- audit/s128_open_roots.tsv has open/partial high-fanout laws R-NEW-001 (MessageQueue enqueue order/IdleHandler/barriers/quit), R-NEW-015 (class initialization/resolution flag matrix), R-NEW-017 (reflection declared/inherited member walk), R-NEW-034 (locale/resource qualifier selection), and R-NEW-068 (layer-list/inset/rotate drawable handling). These are leads to revalidate, not proof of current defects.

## Track 1 — R-NEW-001 MessageQueue/Looper dispatch law (P0, possible many-app lifecycle hangs)
**Problem hypothesis:** incorrect enqueue ordering, due-time selection, synchronization-barrier handling, IdleHandler dispatch, callback removal identity, or quit semantics can prevent Activity/navigation/render callbacks from reaching their expected stage, yielding splash/blank frames despite a live process.
**Work:** inspect current MessageQueue/Looper implementation and trace each queue transition; build minimal deterministic fixtures for now/past/future messages, same-time ordering, delayed callbacks, IdleHandler, barrier bypass, removeCallbacks identity, and quit/quitSafely. Cross-check AOSP source and a Chinese/Russian implementation discussion if useful, but AOSP + local fixture is authority.
**Acceptance:** identify the first failed queue invariant in at least two unrelated real APKs (e.g. one View app + one Compose/game) before changing code. If current law is correct, reject this hypothesis with a trace and select a replacement. Any fix must prove callbacks and a visible app-owned next frame, not just queue unit tests.

## Track 2 — F-NEW-159 null framework receiver contracts (P0, lifecycle-wide)
**Problem evidence:** historical trace has LocaleList.toLanguageTags and WindowInsetsController.setSystemBarsAppearance invoked on null during onCreate. This may be missing framework-owned receiver construction/context propagation; never paper over it with arbitrary non-null defaults.
**Work:** inspect the current receiver-creation paths and exact call sites, compare with AOSP Configuration, Window, WindowInsetsController contracts. Build null/valid receiver fixtures and replay current-head traces for the documented app family.
**Acceptance:** correct object ownership/initialization order, prove legal null still throws where appropriate, then show lifecycle completion and content in at least two affected unrelated apps. If now fixed/superseded, prove on current HEAD and do not duplicate the fix.

## Track 3 — F-NEW-157 GLSurfaceView/EGL/swapBuffers software-surface contract (P0/P1, libGDX/custom surface games)
**Problem evidence:** graphics registry says a plain GLSurfaceView ladder reaches a white screenshot with zero API calls; Surface creation → EGL context → swapBuffers → composition is absent. This is a distinct rendering backend boundary, not a Canvas wrapper bug.
**Work:** trace SurfaceHolder callbacks, GL thread startup, EGL context/config/surface creation, viewport, buffer swap, and host composition. Research AOSP GLSurfaceView/EGL and CPU-compatible translation paths (e.g. SwiftShader architecture) in English plus Chinese/Russian sources. Do not pretend native GPU execution exists if the chosen supported path is a software fallback.
**Acceptance:** first define a minimal deterministic software-surface contract; prove one plain GLSurfaceView fixture and at least two unrelated games (prioritize x86/x86_64 APKs) present nonblank app-owned pixels. If a complete GL backend is too large, implement a scoped but truthful milestone and report the exact remaining boundary—do not count zero-API-call runs as success.

## Track 4 — Arrays.toString null contract (Asteroids Revenge launch path) + separately audit F-111 inflater class-name law
**Problem evidence:** differential white-screen report records Asteroids Revenge returning null from an Arrays.toString shadow; Kotlin Intrinsics then throws before GodotView is created. The trigger may be a Java-library shadow/dispatch defect, not a renderer problem. F-111 separately tracks inflater <view class=...> class-name resolution and must not be conflated with this defect.
**Work:** inspect every Arrays.toString overload and the native/interpreter bridge return-type handling; build fixtures for object arrays, every primitive-array overload, null array semantics, empty arrays, nested arrays, and descriptor/overload dispatch. Confirm whether F-111 inflater class-name law is still open and relevant to current apps; only bundle it if a shared class-name resolution defect is independently proven.
**Acceptance:** correct Java result semantics and non-null return for non-null arrays are proven; Asteroids progresses past the exact previous call site, and at least one other unrelated app exercising the same bridge remains regression-green. Do not claim a whole Godot game renders if its native engine still cannot start.

## Track 5 — R-NEW-068 drawable inflation/state resolution (layer-list, inset, rotate)
**Problem evidence:** graphics registry says XML layer-list/inset/rotate drawable support remains pending; absent backgrounds/icons can make screens look blank or incomplete despite a functioning ViewTree. This is a separate resource→Drawable→bounds/state→Canvas path.
**Work:** trace XML resource selection, drawable object construction, intrinsic dimensions, bounds propagation, state/tint, and draw invocation. Create fixtures for nested layer-list, inset offsets, rotation/pivot, state selector, invalid child/resource and density variants. Compare with AOSP Drawable/LayerDrawable/InsetDrawable/RotateDrawable semantics and multilingual references.
**Acceptance:** exact fixture pixel assertions plus at least three unrelated real apps with visible improvements; verify no ImageView src/background conflation and no resource fallback that masks a missing resource. If these drawables are already fixed on current HEAD, replace this track with the next repeated first-divergence from the live corpus.

## Mandatory execution and evidence
- First synchronize origin/main; record exact HEAD, clean tree, binary SHA-256, registry SHA/count. Current historical reports mention different HEADs, so stale evidence is not acceptable.
- Each track must end as ROOT_CAUSED_FIXED, CONFIRMED_NOT_FIXED, REJECTED_WITH_EVIDENCE, or BLOCKED. “Read source”, “registered”, and “unit test green” are not root fixes.
- For any fix: pre-fix reproduction, exact first divergence, source/algorithm/semantic law, minimal positive + negative tests, post-fix binary SHA, screenshot SHA-256 + pixel census, runtime provenance, and three runs. Group by shared root and target at least 5 candidate APKs per relevant family when available.
- Prioritize x86/x86_64; mark ARM-only cases as prerequisite mismatch, not runtime rendering failures. Run at least 10 valid real APKs across these tracks if corpus/artifacts permit; distinguish launch content from interactive content.
- Preserve wall A/B zero drift, goldens, negatives, reinstall, c72priv/privacy, MG-310, MG-150, and s82 validator. No app-specific package branches, no golden updates to hide regressions, no fake-success screenshots.
- Search authoritative English AOSP sources plus Chinese/Russian GitHub/source discussions. Cite URLs and state exactly which upstream contract applies locally; upstream anecdotes alone do not establish MiniAndroid's root.
- Push source, fixtures, evidence, registry/worklist and report to origin/main. Add one concise #364 scoreboard: the five roots, real apps improved, interactive wins, blank apps remaining, gates, and unproven claims.

**Wave success means:** multiple unrelated real apps advance beyond their previous first-missing stage and show app-owned pixels, with no regression. If fewer than five are truly fixable in this wave, still report five evidence-backed verdicts and clearly mark unimplemented/blocked tracks—never inflate the fixed count.
